(فَاللَّهُ هُوَ الْوَلِيُّ وَهُوَ يُحْيِ الْمَوْتى وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): there is disagreement about this fāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī said it is the answer to an implied condition, i.e. the faṣīḥa fāʾ, as though it were said, after denying every protector other than Him: "If they want a true protector, then Allah is the Protector in truth; there is no protector besides Him in anything." Abū Ḥayyān said in reply to al-Zamakhsharī: "There is no need for this implied element, since the statement is complete without it", i.e. it is merely for conjunction, i.e. conjoining what follows it to what precedes it. Most of the grammarians followed Abū Ḥayyān, and al-Jalāl stated explicitly that it is merely for conjunction. In my view, al-Zamakhsharī's opinion is sounder and closer to the coherence of the parts of the statement with one another. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ, or a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; (الولي) is the khabar of (هو), and the clause is the khabar of (الله) — or [(الولي) is] the khabar of (الله), the separating pronoun having no position. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (يحيي الموتى) the khabar; and (وهو على كل شيء قدير) is likewise conjoined to what preceded.

dervis-irab:10-12.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَذْرَؤُكُمْ): in al-Qāmūs he said: "Dharaʾa, like jaʿala: he created; and [dharaʾa] the thing: he multiplied it; and from it is al-dhurriyya (progeny), with the three vowels [on the dhāl], for the offspring of the two weighty ones (al-thaqalān, i.e. humans and jinn)." Its commentator said in al-Tāj: "It is sometimes applied also to fathers and forebears; Allah the Exalted said: 'We carried their progeny (dhurriyyatahum) in the laden ship'; and the plural is dharārī, like sarārī." What is to be said about it has preceded, and the meaning of its being made transitive with (في) will come in the section on i'rab.
(مَقالِيدُ): its discussion has preceded in Sūrat al-Zumar, so refresh your acquaintance with it.

* I'rab:
(وَمَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, brought to relate the saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the believers, i.e. whatever the disbelievers have opposed you in, in any matter of religion or of this world, the judgement of that disputed matter is entrusted to Allah the Exalted. (ما) is conditional, in the position of nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject), and it may also be relative; (اختلفتم) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (فيه) is attached to (اختلفتم); (من شيء) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʾ is linking; (حكمه) is a mubtadaʾ; and (إلى الله) is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate), i.e. "referred back and returning to Allah". (ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبِّي عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ): (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ and (الله) the khabar — it may also be a badal (substitute) from (ذلكم); (ربي) is a second khabar; (عليه) is attached to (توكلت), and the clause is a third khabar; (إليه) is attached to (أنيب), and the clause is a fourth khabar. (فاطِرُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): a fifth khabar. It has been read in the genitive: Abū al-Baqāʾ said it is a badal from the hāʾ in (عليه), and al-Zamakhsharī said it is a naʿt (adjective) of His saying (فحكمه إلى الله) [Translator's note: i.e. of the name (الله) in it], so that the clause (ذلكم…) etc. is parenthetical between the qualified noun and its adjective. (جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْواجاً وَمِنَ الْأَنْعامِ أَزْواجاً يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ): the clause is a sixth khabar. (جعل) is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; (لكم) is in the position of the second object if it means "to make into", and is attached to (جعل) if it means "to create"; (من أنفسكم) is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of (أزواجا); (أزواجا) is the first object of (جعل); (ومن الأنعام أزواجا) is conjoined to the preceding one; the clause (يذرؤكم) is an adjective of (أزواجا); and (فيه) is attached to (يذرؤكم), the pronoun referring back to the making or the arranging. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: What is the meaning of (يذرؤكم فيه), and why was it not said 'He multiplies you by it'? I say: He made this arrangement like the spring and the mine for spreading and multiplying. Do you not see that you say of animals that in the creation of pairs there is multiplication, as Allah the Exalted said: «ولكم في القصاص حياة»?" (لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ): a seventh khabar. (ليس) is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb; the kāf is redundant (zāʾida); (مثله) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative (manṣūb) in position because it is the khabar of (ليس); and (شيء) is its noun. What we have followed is the view of most of the grammarians, and it is the well-known one among the grammarians; there are interesting, lengthy discussions on this matter which we defer to the section on benefits. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (السميع البصير) are two khabars of (هو). (لَهُ مَقالِيدُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): (له) is a fronted khabar; (مقاليد السموات والأرض) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and the clause is an eighth khabar. (يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ إِنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ)
The clause (يبسط الرزق) is a ninth khabar. (يبسط) is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "He"; (الرزق) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لمن) is attached to (يبسط); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); (يقدر) is conjoined to (يشاء) [Translator's note: so in the source; in sense it is conjoined to (يبسط)]; (إن) and its noun; (عليم) is its khabar; and (بكل شيء) is attached to (عليم).

* Benefits:
On His saying (لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ) there is much disagreement among the great grammarians. We shall present here a summary of all their views, while the easiest of the aspects is what we mentioned, transmitting from the majority of them. Shaykh Bahāʾ al-Dīn ibn al-Naḥḥās said in his commentary on al-Muqarrib: Most people said it [the kāf] is redundant for emphasis, and the meaning — and Allah knows best — is "nothing is like Him". A group of the meticulous scholars said it is not redundant but has its proper sense, and the meaning of the statement — and Allah knows best — is the negation of a like of the like, and from that the negation of the like follows necessarily, given that He, glorified be He, exists. If it is said: Why did He arrive at negating the like by negating the like of the like, and why did He not negate the like at the outset? The answer is that negating the like by negating the like of the like is more eloquent and weightier — [just as "someone like you does not do this" is weightier] than our saying "you do not do this" — because it negates the thing by mentioning its proof, and that is more eloquent than negating the thing without mentioning its proof.
I say: Some of them said that it is not redundant, and did not rely on this proof; rather they said that mithl and mathal, with sukūn and with a vowel, are the same in the language, like shibh and shabah; so mithl here means mathal (attribute). Allah the Exalted said: «ولله المثل الأعلى»; and the meaning would be "nothing is like His attribute", and that is correct.
Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as Ibn al-Samīn, said: "His saying (ليس كمثله شيء): in this verse there are several aspects. The first, which is the well-known one among the grammarians, is that the kāf is redundant in the khabar of (ليس), (شيء) is its noun, and the implied form is 'nothing is like Him'. They said: Were it not for claiming that it is redundant, it would follow that He has a like, which is impossible, since the implied form, if the kāf were original, would become 'nothing is like His like'; this negates likeness from His like, and so establishes that He has a like and that that like has no like — and this is impossible; Allah is exalted far above that. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: If it were not redundant, that would lead to the impossible, since the meaning would be that He has a like and that His like has no like, and in that there is a contradiction, because if He has a like then His like has a like, namely He Himself — in addition to which affirming a like for Allah the Exalted is impossible. I say: This is a strange method of establishing the redundancy, but it is a method of fine craftsmanship. The second: that it is (مثل) which is redundant, as it is redundant in the saying of Allah the Exalted (بمثل ما آمنتم). Al-Ṭabarī said: just as the kāf is made redundant in some places. This is not good, because the redundancy of nouns is not permissible, and also the implied form would become 'nothing is like Him (ka-huwa)', and the entry of the kāf on pronouns is not permissible except in poetry. The third: that the Arabs say 'someone like you does not do such-and-such', meaning the addressee himself, because they want to intensify the negation of the description from the addressee, so they negate it in wording from his like, and its absence from him is thereby established with its proof. Ibn Qutayba said:
The Arabs put 'the like' in the place of 'the self', and say 'someone like me is not spoken to like this', i.e. I am not spoken to like this. The fourth: that by mithl is meant the attribute, that is, mithl in the sense of mathal, and mathal is the attribute, as in His saying (مثل الجنة); so the meaning would be: nothing among the attributes belonging to others is like the attribute of Allah the Exalted. This is an easy interpretation."
Al-Rāghib, in his Mufradāt, has subtle words that are worth recording here about al-mithl; he said:
"Al-mithl is the most general of the words coined for resemblance. That is because nidd is said of what shares in substance only, shibh is said of what shares with it in quantity and extent only, and mithl in all of that. For this reason, when Allah wanted to negate resemblance in every respect, He singled it out for mention; Allah the Exalted said: (ليس كمثله شيء)."
Ibn Hishām al-Anṣārī said in his delightful book al-Mughnī: "Most said the implied form is 'nothing is like Him', since if it were not taken as redundant the meaning would become 'nothing is like His like', and an impossibility would follow, namely affirming a like. It was made redundant only to emphasize the negation of a like, because the redundancy of a particle is equivalent to repeating the clause a second time — Ibn Jinnī said that — and because when they intensify the negation of an action from someone they say 'someone like you does not do such-and-such', while what they mean is only the negation from his very self; but when they negate it from one who has his most specific attributes, they have negated it from him. It has been said that the kāf in the verse is not redundant; then there was disagreement: it was said that the redundant one is (مثل), as it is made redundant in «فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم»; they said it was made redundant here only to separate the kāf from the pronoun. End. The view that the particle is redundant is better than the view that the noun is redundant; indeed the redundancy of nouns has not been established."
We conclude this discussion with al-Zamakhsharī's words in his Kashshāf — and "Juhayza has cut off the speech of every orator" [Translator's note: a proverb meaning that the final word has been said] — he said: "They said: 'Someone like you is not miserly', negating miserliness from his like while meaning to negate it from his very self. They intended intensification in that, so they took the path of kināya (allusion) with it, because when they negate it from one who takes his place and who has his most specific attributes, they have negated it from him. Its parallel is your saying to an Arab: 'The Arabs do not violate covenants' — this is more eloquent than your saying 'you do not violate'. From it is their saying: 'His peers have reached adolescence and his age-mates have come of age', meaning his own adolescence and coming of age. And in the ḥadīth of Ruqayqa bint Ṣayfī concerning the rain-prayer of ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib: 'Behold, among them is the one whose peers are good and pure', the intent being his own purity and goodness. Once it is known that it is of the category of kināya, there is no difference between His saying 'nothing is like Allah' and His saying (ليس كمثله شيء) except the benefit that kināya gives; it is as though they are two expressions succeeding one another upon one meaning, namely the negation of likeness from His very self. Similar is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: «بل يداه مبسوطتان», for its meaning is 'rather, He is generous', without conceiving of a hand or its extension, because it has become an expression for generosity, by which they intend nothing else — so much so that they have used it of one who has no hand. Likewise this has been used of one who has a like and of one who has no like. You may also claim that the word of comparison has been repeated for emphasis, as it was repeated by the one who said:
وصاليات ككما يؤثفين
(and fire-blackened stones, like as they are set as hearthstones)
and by the one who said:
فأصبحت مثل كعصف مأكول
(and they became like as straw eaten up)."
Al-Qāḍī Ibn al-Munayyir commented on al-Zamakhsharī's words, saying: "This second aspect is to be rejected, in addition to the damage it does to the meaning. That is because what is fitting here is to emphasize the negation of likeness, whereas on this aspect the kāf only emphasizes the likeness; and there is a difference between emphasizing a negated likeness and emphasizing the negation of likeness. Negating a likeness left free of emphasis is more eloquent and more emphatic in meaning than negating a likeness coupled with emphasis, since from negating a non-emphasized likeness the negation of every likeness follows, whereas from negating a verified, emphasized, intensive likeness the negation of a likeness lesser than it in verification and emphasis does not follow. And wherever the kāf has occurred emphasizing likeness [Translator's note: the source prints «للماثلة», a misprint for «للمماثلة»], it has occurred in affirmation and emphasized it" — until he says: "The aspect that he mentioned [first] is the correct aspect in the verse in his view, and he signalled the weakness of this second aspect by his words 'You may also claim'; so understand."

dervis-irab:13-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَجْتَبِي إِلَيْهِ): He draws to Himself. Al-ijtibāʾ is the iftiʿāl form from al-jibāya, which is gathering. Al-Rāghib said: One says jabaytu al-māʾa fī al-ḥawḍ, i.e. I gathered the water in the basin; and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «يجبى إليه ثمرات كل شيء». Al-ijtibāʾ is gathering by way of choosing; Allah the Exalted said: «قالوا لولا اجتبيتها». Allah's choosing (ijtibāʾ) of the servant is His singling him out with a divine outpouring [Translator's note: the source prints «بغيض», a misprint for «بفيض», "outpouring"], so that various kinds of blessings come to him without striving on his part.

* I'rab:
(شَرَعَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الدِّينِ ما وَصَّى بِهِ نُوحاً وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنا إِلَيْكَ): you may make it a tenth khabar (predicate), and you may make it a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement brought to begin detailing what He first stated in summary. (شرع) is a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; (لكم) is attached to (شرع); (من الدين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (وصى) is the ṣila (relative clause); (به) is attached to (وصى); (نوحا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (الذي) is conjoined to (ما); the clause (أوحينا) is the ṣila; and (إليك) is attached to (أوحينا). (وَما وَصَّيْنا بِهِ إِبْراهِيمَ وَمُوسى وَعِيسى): also conjoined to what preceded. These five prophets are singled out for mention because of their eminence and high standing, since they are the Messengers of Resolve (ulū al-ʿazm min al-rusul). (أَنْ أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ): (أن) is explicative (tafsīriyya), in the sense of "that is", because it is preceded by something that contains the meaning of saying without its letters, namely (وصى). It may also be maṣdariyya (infinitival), interpreted together with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is: that you establish"; or in the position of accusative as a badal (substitute) from the relative noun, namely (ما); or in the position of genitive as a badal from (الدين). (أقيموا الدين) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is conjunctive; (لا) is prohibitive; (تتفرقوا) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لا); and (فيه) is attached to (تتفرقوا). (كَبُرَ عَلَى الْمُشْرِكِينَ ما تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يُنِيبُ): a resumptive statement. (كبر) is a past verb; (على المشركين) is attached to (كبر); (ما) is the fāʿil; the clause (تدعوهم) is the ṣila; (إليه) is attached to (تدعوهم); (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يجتبي) is the khabar; (إليه) is attached to (يهدي) [Translator's note: so in the source; this first (إليه) belongs to (يجتبي)]; (من) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila; (يهدي) is conjoined to (يجتبي); (إليه) is attached to (يهدي); (من) is a mafʿūl bihi; and the clause (ينيب) is the ṣila. (وَما تَفَرَّقُوا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْياً بَيْنَهُمْ): a resumptive statement brought to begin explaining the state of the People of the Book after the summary reference to the states of the people of polytheism. (ما) is negating; (تفرقوا) is a past verb and its fāʿil; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (من بعد) is attached to (تفرقوا), and the exception is from the most general of states, so it is also attached to an omitted ḥāl; (ما) is maṣdariyya, interpreted together with what falls within its scope as a maṣdar annexed to the adverb; (جاءهم العلم) is a past verb, a mafʿūl bihi and a fāʿil; and (بغيا) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), or a maṣdar interpreted as a derived word, so it is accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "transgressing"; and (بينهم) is attached to (بغيا). I.e. their splitting was not due to any shortcoming in the clarification and the proofs, but due to transgression [Translator's note: the source prints «للبعي», a misprint for «للبغي»], wrongdoing and preoccupation with this world. (وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; (لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence because of existence; (كلمة) is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the clause (سبقت) is a naʿt (adjective) of (كلمة); (من ربك) is attached to (سبقت); (إلى أجل) is attached to (سبقت); (مسمى) is a naʿt of (أجل); the lām occurs in the answer of (لولا); (قضي) is a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the maṣdar understood from (قضي), i.e. "the judgement"; (بينهم) is attached to (قضي); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. (وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُورِثُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ لَفِي شَكٍّ مِنْهُ مُرِيبٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, and you may make it circumstantial (ḥāliyya), explaining the manner of the polytheists' disbelief in the Qur'an. (إن) and its noun; the clause (أورثوا) is the ṣila; (أورثوا) is a passive past verb, the wāw being the nāʾib fāʿil and (الكتاب) the second mafʿūl bihi; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (في شك) is the khabar of (إن); (منه) is a naʿt of (شك); and (مريب) is a second naʿt. (فَلِذلِكَ فَادْعُ وَاسْتَقِمْ كَما أُمِرْتَ): the faṣīḥa fāʾ; (لذلك) is attached to (ادع); the second fāʾ emphasizes the first fāʾ; and the lām is in the sense of "to", i.e. "if you have come to know all this and grasped the sources of the splitting, then call to agreement upon the ḥanīf religion". (استقم) is conjoined to (ادع); the kāf is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar; and (ما) may be maṣdariyya or relative. Al-istiqāma is keeping to the straight course; what is to be said about the straight line has preceded, and that the slightest deviation takes it out of the bounds of its straightness. (وَلا تَتَّبِعْ أَهْواءَهُمْ وَقُلْ آمَنْتُ بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنْ كِتابٍ): the wāw is conjunctive; (لا) is prohibitive; (تتبع) is an imperfect verb, jussive by (لا), its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you"; (أهواءهم) is a mafʿūl bihi; (قل) is an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being "you"; the clause (آمنت) is the maqūl al-qawl (the content of the saying); (بما) is attached to (آمنت); the clause (أنزل الله) is the ṣila, the referent being omitted, i.e. "Allah sent it down"; and (من كتاب) is a ḥāl. (وَأُمِرْتُ لِأَعْدِلَ بَيْنَكُمُ): conjoined to (آمنت). The lām is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra); (أعدل) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (أن) after the lām of outcome; and (بينكم) is an adverb attached to (أعدل). This is safer than the statement of al-Jalāl and his commentators that the lām is in the sense of the bāʾ and that the maṣdariyya (أن) is implied, since we have not seen the lām occur in the sense of the bāʾ, and none of the grammarians has mentioned that the maṣdariyya (أن) is implied after the bāʾ. What is meant is only that the command leads to justice among you. (اللَّهُ رَبُّنا وَرَبُّكُمْ لَنا أَعْمالُنا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمالُكُمْ): the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ and (ربنا) its khabar; (لكم) [Translator's note: i.e. (وربكم)] is conjoined to (ربنا); (لنا) is a fronted khabar and (أعمالنا) a delayed mubtadaʾ; (لكم) is a fronted khabar and (أعمالكم) a delayed mubtadaʾ. (لا حُجَّةَ بَيْنَنا وَبَيْنَكُمُ اللَّهُ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنا وَإِلَيْهِ الْمَصِيرُ): (لا) is the lā of generic negation; (حجة) is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; and (بيننا) is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar, i.e. "there is no dispute between us and you", because falsehood is stammering and truth is radiant; the truth has appeared and you have been defeated in argument, so there is no point in bringing forward arguments. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يجمع) is the khabar; (بيننا) is an adverb attached to (يجمع), i.e. on the Day of Resurrection; (إليه) is a fronted khabar; and (المصير) is a delayed mubtadaʾ.

* Benefits:
1- The lām of cause or of outcome: the imperfect is made accusative by (أن) implied optionally after the genitive-governing lām, which is called the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl) or the lām of consequence and outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba wa-l-ṣayrūra), as in «وأمرنا لنسلم لرب العالمين». It is permissible to make (أن) overt, as in «وأمرت لأن أكون أول المسلمين». If the lām is preceded by negated kāna, the implying of (أن) is obligatory, and the lām is called the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); its discussion has preceded.
2- The Messengers of Resolve (ulū al-ʿazm min al-rusul): the meaning of "the Messengers of Resolve" is those who bore hardships and were patient with the harm that befell them from their peoples after they undertook to guide them. Someone has gathered them in his saying:
محمد إبراهيم موسى كليمه ... فعيسى فنوح هم أولو العزم فاعلم
(Muḥammad, Ibrāhīm, Mūsā who spoke with Him, then ʿĪsā, then Nūḥ: they are the Messengers of Resolve — so know it.)

dervis-irab:16-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(داحِضَةٌ): void. In al-Mukhtār: daḥaḍat ḥujjatuhu: his argument became void, its pattern being khaḍaʿa; and Allah adḥaḍahā (made it void). Daḥaḍat rijluhu: his foot slipped, its pattern being qaṭaʿa; al-idḥāḍ is causing to slip. Al-daḥḍ — with fatḥa on the dāl and sukūn on the ḥāʾ, both undotted, and also with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, its last letter being the dotted ḍād — is slipperiness. In a ḥadīth that Aḥmad narrated from Abū Asmāʾ: "He entered upon Abū Dharr while he was at al-Rabadha, and with him was a black woman, unkempt, with no trace of adornment or of perfume (khalūq) on her. He said: 'Will you not look at what this little black woman is ordering me to do? She orders me to go to Iraq; and if I go to Iraq they will incline towards me with their worldly goods. My bosom friend ﷺ charged me that before the bridge of Hell there is a path with slipperiness (daḥḍ) and a place of slipping, and that our coming upon it with moderation and leanness in our loads is more likely to be saved [Translator's note: the source has «ينجو», "he is saved"; the sense is "for us to be saved"] than our coming upon it heavily laden.'"
(مُشْفِقُونَ): fearful.

* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ يُحَاجُّونَ فِي اللَّهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما اسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ حُجَّتُهُمْ داحِضَةٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ): (والذين) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause (يحاجون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (في الله) is attached to (يحاجون), and it is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "concerning the religion of Allah"; (من بعد) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (ما) is maṣdariyya (infinitival), interpreted together with what falls within its scope as a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to the adverb; (له) is in the position of nominative as the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of (استجيب), or it is attached to it with the nāʾib fāʿil latent (mustatir); (حجتهم) is a mubtadaʾ; (داحضة) is the khabar (predicate) of (حجتهم), and the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ, which is the relative noun; and (عند ربهم) is an adverb attached to (داحضة). (وَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌ وَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; (عليهم) is a fronted khabar and (غضب) a delayed mubtadaʾ; (لهم) is a fronted khabar and (عذاب) a delayed mubtadaʾ; and (شديد) is a naʿt (adjective) of (عذاب). (اللَّهُ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ وَالْمِيزانَ): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (الذي) its khabar; the clause (أنزل الكتاب) is the ṣila; (بالحق) is attached to (أنزل), the bāʾ being for accompaniment (mulābasa), or to an omitted ḥāl; and (الميزان) is conjoined to (الحق) [Translator's note: so in the source; in the verse (الميزان) is accusative and conjoined to (الكتاب)]. (وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as the mubtadaʾ; the clause (يدريك) is the khabar; (لعل), its noun and its khabar; and the clause (لعل الساعة قريب) is the second object of (أدري) [Translator's note: i.e. of the verb adrā, of which (يدريك) is the imperfect], because it has been suspended (ʿulliqa) from operation by the expression of hope. A muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "perhaps the coming of the Hour is near". One may not say that in (قريب) masculine and feminine are the same, because faʿīl here is in the sense of fāʿil, not in the sense of mafʿūl. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It may be put in the masculine on the sense of 'time', or on the sense of 'resurrection', or on [the sense of] relation, i.e. possessing nearness." I say: They likened the faʿīl that means fāʿil to the one that means mafʿūl and dropped the tāʾ from it; an instance of that is the saying of Allah the Exalted «إن رحمة الله قريب من المحسنين», which is in the sense of muqtarib (drawing near); they likened it to qatīl (killed) and the like. It has also been said that the tāʾ was dropped from it only because al-raḥma (mercy) and al-ruḥm are one, so they construed the khabar according to the sense; this is supported by the saying of Allah the Exalted «هذا رحمة من ربي». The discussion of what is the same for masculine and feminine will come in the section on benefits. (يَسْتَعْجِلُ بِهَا الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِها): (يستعجل) is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb; (بها) is attached to (يستعجل); (الذين) is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause (لا يؤمنون بها) is the ṣila. (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مُشْفِقُونَ مِنْها وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهَا الْحَقُّ): the wāw is conjunctive; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (مشفقون) is the khabar; (منها) is attached to (مشفقون); the wāw is conjunctive; (يعلمون) is a nominative imperfect verb; and (أن) and what falls within its scope takes the place of the two objects of (يعلمون). (أَلا إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُمارُونَ فِي السَّاعَةِ لَفِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ): (ألا) is a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh); (إن) and its noun; the clause (يمارون) is the ṣila; (في الساعة) is attached to (يمارون). Al-mumārāh is wrangling [Translator's note: the source prints «الملاجة»; «الملاجّة», "persistent disputing", is evidently intended], because each one of them "yamrī" (draws out) what his companion has, i.e. extracts it. The lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (في ضلال) is the khabar of (إن); and (بعيد) is a naʿt of (ضلال). (اللَّهُ لَطِيفٌ بِعِبادِهِ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَهُوَ الْقَوِيُّ الْعَزِيزُ): (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (لطيف) the khabar; (بعباده) is attached to (لطيف); the clause (يرزق) is a second khabar; (من) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila; the wāw is a conjunction; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, (القوي) the khabar and (العزيز) a second khabar.

* Benefits:
When masculine and feminine are the same. Masculine and feminine are the same in five patterns:
1- Faʿūl, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, in the sense of fāʿil, as in rajul ṣabūr (a patient man), meaning ṣābir, and imraʾa ṣabūr (a patient woman), meaning ṣābira. As for their saying imraʾa malūla, from al-malal (boredom), meaning mālla, the tāʾ in it is not for distinguishing [gender] but for intensification, by the evidence of its entering the masculine, as in rajul malūla. As for imraʾa ʿaduwwa (a woman enemy), it is anomalous (shādhdh) because it departs from the rule; nevertheless it is construed on the analogy of ṣadīqa (female friend), just as in its converse ṣadīq (friend) is construed on the analogy of ʿaduww in his saying "while you are a friend (ṣadīq)", where the analogical form would be ṣadīqa; they construe an opposite on its opposite just as they construe a like on its like. If faʿūl is in the sense of mafʿūl, the distinguishing tāʾ may optionally be attached to it, as in jamal rakūb (a riding camel) and nāqa rakūba (a riding she-camel). ʿAntara said:
فيها اثنتان وأربعون حلوبة ... سودا كخافية الغراب الأعصم
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the hidden wing-feathers of the white-footed raven.)
2- Faʿīl in the sense of mafʿūl, as in rajul jarīḥ (a wounded man) and imraʾa jarīḥ (a wounded woman), meaning majrūḥa. Milḥafa jadīda (a new wrapper), with the tāʾ, is anomalous, for it means majdūda, yet the tāʾ has been attached to it. If faʿīl is in the sense of fāʿil, the distinguishing tāʾ is attached to it, as in imraʾa raḥīma (a merciful woman) and ẓarīfa (a charming woman). If you say "I passed by the slain woman (qatīla) of Banū so-and-so", you attach the tāʾ for fear of confusion between masculine and feminine, because you have not mentioned the qualified noun with which confusion would be safely avoided.
3- Mifʿāl, with kasra on the mīm: minḥār; one says rajul minḥār and imraʾa minḥār, i.e. one who slaughters [camels] much. Mīqāna, from al-yaqīn, which is the absence of hesitation, is anomalous; one says rajul mīqān, one who hears nothing without being certain of it, and imraʾa mīqāna.
4- Faʿīl [Translator's note: so in the source; the pattern meant is mifʿīl, as the description "with kasra on the mīm" and the example show], with kasra on the mīm, as in miʿṭīr (much perfumed), from al-ʿiṭr. Imraʾa miskīna (a poor woman) is anomalous because it departs from the rule; nevertheless it is construed on the analogy of faqīra. Imraʾa miskīn has been heard, according to the analogy; Sībawayh related it.
5- Mifʿal, with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn, as in mighsham, one who does not desist from what he wants and desires, out of his courage; and midʿas, from al-daʿs, which is thrusting [with a spear].

dervis-irab:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(مَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الْآخِرَةِ نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, brought to explain the difference between the deeds of the two kinds of workers: whoever works for the Hereafter is granted success in his work and his good deeds are multiplied, while whoever's work is for this world is given something of it — not what he wants and aspires to — and has no share in the Hereafter. (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of nominative as the mubtadaʾ (subject); (كان) is a past verb, its noun referring back to (من); the clause (يريد) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان); (حرث الآخرة) is the object of (يريد); (نزد) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (له) is attached to (نزد); and (في حرثه) is also attached to (نزد). (وَمَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدُّنْيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْها وَما لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ نَصِيبٍ): the clause (وَمَنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدُّنْيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنْها) is conjoined to the preceding clause. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or conjunctive; (ما) is negating, and it may be Ḥijāzī according to those who permit the fronting of the khabar; (له) is a fronted khabar; (في الآخرة) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (نصيب) is a mubtadaʾ or the noun of (ما). (أَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكاءُ شَرَعُوا لَهُمْ مِنَ الدِّينِ ما لَمْ يَأْذَنْ بِهِ اللَّهُ): some took (أم) as implying the bal of transition (bal al-intiqāliyya), and al-Zamakhsharī took it as implying bal plus the hamza, for reproach and rebuke. (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (شركاء) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause (شرعوا) is a naʿt (adjective) of (شركاء); (لهم) is attached to (شرعوا); (من الدين) is a ḥāl, because it was an adjective of the object, i.e. "a law of religion", what is meant by it being the polytheism that Allah has not permitted; (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause (لم يأذن) is the ṣila (relative clause); (به) is attached to (يأذن); and (الله) is the fāʿil (agent). (وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةُ الْفَصْلِ لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ)
The wāw is conjunctive; (لولا) is a particle of non-occurrence because of existence; (كلمة الفصل) is a mubtadaʾ, the khabar being omitted; the lām occurs in the answer of (لولا); and the clause (قضي بينهم) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَإِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; (إن) and its noun; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (عذاب) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; (أليم) is a naʿt; and the clause (لهم عذاب أليم) is the khabar of (إن).

* Rhetoric:
The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying «من كان يريد حرث الآخرة» — the verse — there is an explicit metaphor. What the worker does, seeking benefit and growth by it, is likened to tillage (al-ḥarth). Al-ḥarth is originally casting seed into the ground, and it is applied to the crop that results from it. Then the thing likened, namely the work, is omitted, and that to which it is likened, namely the tillage, is retained, to indicate the results and fruits of deeds. He likened it to crops in that it is a benefit obtained by work in this world; for that reason it has been said: "This world is the sowing-field of the Hereafter."

dervis-irab:22-23.t:
* I'rab:
(تَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا وَهُوَ واقِعٌ بِهِمْ): the address is to everyone from whom seeing can come. (الظالمين) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (مشفقين) is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual; (مما) is attached to (مشفقين); the clause (كسبوا) is the ṣila (relative clause); the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (واقع) the khabar (predicate); (بهم) is attached to (واقع); and the clause is a second ḥāl, the pronoun referring back to what they earned or to the fearing. (وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فِي رَوْضاتِ الْجَنَّاتِ): (والذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا); and (في روضات الجنات) is the khabar. (لَهُمْ ما يَشاؤُنَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ): (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (ما) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; the clause (يشاءون) is the ṣila; (عند ربهم) is an adverb of the [notion of] being established that governs (لهم), and it may be an adverb of (يشاءون), though al-Zamakhsharī disallowed the second. (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ; (الفضل) is the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar is the khabar of the first; (الكبير) is a naʿt (adjective); and you may make (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. (ذلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ عِبادَهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and (الذين) [Translator's note: so in the source; (الذي) is meant] its khabar; the clause (يبشر الله عباده) is the ṣila, the referent being omitted, i.e. "with which He gives glad tidings to His servants"; (الذين آمنوا) is a naʿt; and (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا). (قُلْ لا أَسْئَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّةَ فِي الْقُرْبى): (قل) is an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), i.e. say, in answer to those who conversed among themselves: "Do you think Muḥammad asks for a wage for what he is engaged in?" (لا) is negating; (أسألكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a first mafʿūl bihi; (عليه) is a ḥāl; (أجرا) is a second mafʿūl bihi; and (إلا المودة) may be a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), i.e. "I do not ask you any wage except this, namely that you show affection to my kinsfolk"; or it may be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), i.e. "I do not ask you any wage at all, but I ask you to show affection to my kinsfolk, who are your kinsfolk". (في القربى) is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "established in kinship"; al-qurbā is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like al-zulfā and al-bushrā. More discussion of this verse will come. (وَمَنْ يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَزِدْ لَهُ فِيها حُسْناً إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ)
The wāw is conjunctive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun and the mubtadaʾ; (يقترف) is an imperfect verb, the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (حسنة) is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. "whoever earns a good deed". The root of al-qarf is earning; one says "so-and-so yaqrifu (earns) a living for his dependants", of the pattern ḍaraba. (نزد) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (له) is attached to (نزد); (فيها) is a ḥāl; (حسنا) is a mafʿūl bihi; (إن), its noun and its two khabars; and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «إلا المودة في القربى» there is a majāz mursal (non-metaphorical trope) whose relation is locality (al-maḥalliyya). For that reason He did not say "except the affection of kinship" or "except affection for kinship"; they [the kinsfolk] have been made a place for affection and an abode for it, as when you say "I have, among the family of so-and-so, affection, and I have among them a strong attachment", meaning "I love them, and they are the place and abode of my love". There has been much disagreement about this verse, which may be consulted in the lengthy works. The best we have read on it is what Mujāhid and Qatāda mentioned, the gist of which is: The meaning is, "You are my people and the most entitled to respond to me and obey me; since you have refused that, then preserve the right of kinship, maintain the ties of kinship with me, and do not harm me."

dervis-irab:24-26.t:
* I'rab:
(أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِباً): (أم) is a conjunction, and it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of "rather"; (يقولون) is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb; the clause (افترى) is the maqūl al-qawl (the content of the saying); (على الله) is attached to (افترى); and (كذبا) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (فَإِنْ يَشَإِ اللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلى قَلْبِكَ): the fāʾ is resumptive or conjunctive; (إن) is conditional; (يشأ) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (الله) is the fāʿil (agent); (يختم) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and (على قلبك) is attached to (يختم). There is disagreement about the meaning of the sealing. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If Allah wills, He will make you one of those whose hearts are sealed, so that you would fabricate a lie against Him; for none dares to fabricate a lie against Allah except one who is in a state like theirs. The upshot of this style is to deem fabrication far-fetched from one like him, and that it is as remote as associating partners with Allah and entering the company of those whose hearts are sealed." This is beautiful speech in which there is an intoxicating breath of eloquence. Al-Jalāl said: "(فإن يشإ الله يختم): He will bind your heart with patience over their harming you with this saying and others; and He has done so. So the willing of the sealing here is certain to occur." This is also beautiful speech, fitting in this context. (وَيَمْحُ اللَّهُ الْباطِلَ وَيُحِقُّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, not included in the requital of the condition, because Allah the Exalted effaces falsehood absolutely. The wāw has dropped in pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it has dropped in some copies of the Qur'an in writing, construing it according to the pronunciation. [Translator's note: the source says «خطأ», "erroneously" or "in the script"; the word is ambiguous here.] (يمحو الله الباطل) is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; (يحق الحق) is conjoined to (يمحو الله الباطل); (بكلماته) is attached to (يحق); (إن) and its noun; (عليم) is its khabar (predicate); and (بذات الصدور) is attached to (عليم). (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبادِهِ وَيَعْفُوا عَنِ السَّيِّئاتِ وَيَعْلَمُ ما تَفْعَلُونَ): a resumptive statement, brought to explain the acceptance of repentance when it fulfils its three conditions, if the sin is between the servant and his Lord. They are: 1- desisting from the sin; 2- regret for having done it; 3- resolving never to return to it. If the sin concerns the right of a human being, a fourth condition is added to them, namely: 4- that he free himself of the right of its owner. There are lengthy discussions concerning repentance, which may be consulted in the lengthy works. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) the khabar; the clause (يقبل التوبة) is the ṣila (relative clause); (عن عباده) is attached to (التوبة). (عن) here is either in the sense of (من), or else accepting is made transitive to a second object by (من) and (عن) because it contains the sense of taking and of separating: because it contains the sense of taking, it is made transitive with (من) — one says qabiltuhu minhu, i.e. I took it from him; and because it contains the sense of separating and parting, it is made transitive with (عن) — one says qabiltuhu ʿanhu, i.e. I removed it and separated it from him. Some subtle words of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib on repentance will come in the section on benefits. (ويعفو عن السيئات) is conjoined to what preceded, and likewise His saying (ويعلم ما تفعلون); it has also been read with the yāʾ (يفعلون). (وَيَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ): the wāw is conjunctive; (يستجيب) is a nominative imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form referring back to Allah the Exalted; and (الذين) is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. "and He responds to those who believed", the preposition being omitted as it is omitted in His saying «وإذا كالوهم»; i.e. He rewards them for their obedience and gives them more than the reward out of bounty. Al-Samīn permitted the relative noun to be the fāʿil, i.e. they respond to their Lord when He calls them, the sīn and tāʾ being redundant; and he permitted it to be a mafʿūl bihi once the redundancy of the sīn and tāʾ is established, i.e. Allah answers those who believed. The first is more correct. (وعملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا), entering the scope of the ṣila; (يزيدهم) is also conjoined; and (من فضله) is attached to (يزيدهم). To this last [view] al-Suyūṭī and Abū al-Baqāʾ inclined. (وَالْكافِرُونَ لَهُمْ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ): (الكافرون) is a mubtadaʾ; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (عذاب) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; (شديد) is a naʿt (adjective); and the clause is the khabar of (الكافرون).

* Benefits:
Repentance, and a word of our master ʿAlī: Jābir narrated that a Bedouin entered the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You," and said the takbīr. When he had finished his prayer, ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "You there! Quickness of the tongue in seeking forgiveness is the repentance of liars, and your repentance needs repentance." He said: "O Commander of the Believers, and what is repentance?" He said: "It is a name that applies to six meanings: regret for past sins; for neglecting obligatory duties, making them up; returning what was wrongfully taken; melting the self in obedience as you nurtured it in disobedience; making the self taste the bitterness of obedience as you made it taste the sweetness of disobedience; and weeping in place of every laugh you laughed."
Al-Aṣbahānī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The one who regrets awaits mercy from Allah, and the self-admiring awaits hatred. Know, servants of Allah, that every worker will come to his work, and he will not leave this world until he sees the good of his work and the evil of his work; deeds are only by their endings. Night and day are two mounts, so travel well on them to the Hereafter, and beware of procrastination, for death comes suddenly. Let none of you be deluded by the forbearance of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, for Paradise and the Fire are nearer to any one of you than the strap of his sandal. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: «فمن يعمل مثقال ذرة خيرا يره ومن يعمل مثقال ذرة شرا يره»."
The meaning of al-shirāk: one of the straps of the sandal that are on its upper surface. This is by way of approximation and making it understood that bliss and punishment are reached quickly: after the soul departs, the obedient believer sees his reward and the disobedient his punishment. So the intelligent one is he who repents to Allah, hastens in obedience and strives in worship, and none knows the end of life except Allah. The Prophet thus makes the believer desire repentance, in hope of attaining the mercy of Allah and His reward, makes despair hateful to him, and makes him shun arrogance and delusion, as Allah the Exalted said: «اعلموا أنما الحياة الدنيا لعب ولهو وزينة وتفاخر بينكم وتكاثر في الأموال والأولاد كمثل غيث أعجب الكفار نباته ثم يهيج فتراه مصفرا ثم يكون حطاما وفي الآخرة عذاب شديد ومغفرة من الله ورضوان وما الحياة الدنيا إلا متاع الغرور».
Furthermore, al-Mutanabbī portrayed repentance and inclining towards the highest ideal in his delightful saying:
ومن يجد الطريق إلى المعالي ... فلا يذر المطي بلا سنام
(Whoever finds the road to lofty things does not leave his mounts with their humps intact [i.e. he spares no effort].)
ولم أر في عيوب الناس عيبا ... كنقص القادرين على التمام
(And I have not seen among people's faults a fault like the deficiency of those able to reach completeness.)

dervis-irab:27-31.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ): a resumptive (istiʾnāfī) statement, brought to explain that extending provision is a cause of corruption for creatures. (لو) is conditional; (بسط الله الرزق) is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (لعباده) is attached to (بسط); the lām occurs in the answer of (لو); and the clause (بغوا في الأرض) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. A discussion of the meaning of (لو) here, and of the negation of transgression despite its existence, will come in the section on benefits. (وَلكِنْ يُنَزِّلُ بِقَدَرٍ ما يَشاءُ إِنَّهُ بِعِبادِهِ خَبِيرٌ بَصِيرٌ): the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لكن) is a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); (ينزل) is a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He"; (بقدر) is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila (relative clause); (إن) and its noun; (بعباده) is attached to (خبير); and (خبير بصير) are two khabars (predicates) of (إن). (وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ما قَنَطُوا وَيَنْشُرُ رَحْمَتَهُ وَهُوَ الْوَلِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): the wāw is conjunctive; (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and (الذي) its khabar; the clause (ينزل الغيث) is the ṣila; (من بعد) is a ḥāl; (ما) is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and together with what it governs it is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), genitive by annexation to the adverb, i.e. "after their despairing"; (ينشر رحمته) is conjoined to (ينزل الغيث); (هو) is a mubtadaʾ and (الولي الحميد) are its two khabars. (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَما بَثَّ فِيهِما مِنْ دابَّةٍ): the wāw is conjunctive; (من آياته) is a fronted khabar; (خلق السموات والأرض) is a delayed mubtadaʾ; and (ما) is in the position of nominative or genitive: on the first, it is conjoined to the muḍāf, and on the second to the muḍāf ilayhi. This [second] is preferable because it is free of implied elements, since on the first a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. "the creation of what He spread". The clause (بث) is the ṣila; (فيهما) is attached to (بث); and (من دابة) is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. More discussion of this verse will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَهُوَ عَلى جَمْعِهِمْ إِذا يَشاءُ قَدِيرٌ): (وهو) is a mubtadaʾ; (على جمعهم) is attached to (قدير); (إذا) is a future adverb attached to (جمعهم); the clause (يشاء) is in the position of genitive by the annexation of the adverb to it; and (قدير) is the khabar of (هو). (وَما أَصابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُوا عَنْ كَثِيرٍ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is conditional; (أصابكم) is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi, and it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (من مصيبة) is a ḥāl; the fāʾ is linking; (بما) is attached to an omitted khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "then that is because of what [your hands] earned"; (ما) is relative, made genitive by the bāʾ; the clause (كسبت) is the ṣila; and (أيديكم) is the fāʿil. Furthermore, (ما) [the first] may be relative, with the fāʾ entering the khabar by likening the relative to the condition. The wāw is conjunctive; (يعفو) is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, referring back to Allah; and (عن كثير) is attached to (يعفو). (وَما أَنْتُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلا نَصِيرٍ): the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating (mā); (أنتم) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (معجزين) is genitive (majrūr) in form and accusative (manṣūb) in position as the khabar of (ما); (في الأرض) is a ḥāl; the wāw is conjunctive; (ما) is negating, or Ḥijāzī; (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (من دون الله) is a ḥāl; (من) is a redundant preposition; (ولي) is a delayed mubtadaʾ, nominative in position, or the noun of (ما); and (ولا نصير) is conjoined to (من ولي).

* Rhetoric:
1- Ṣiḥḥat al-tafsīr (sound explication): in His saying «وهو الذي ينزل الغيث من بعد ما قنطوا» — the verse — there is the figure of sound explication. It is that the speaker brings, at the beginning of his speech, a meaning whose import understanding cannot grasp on its own: either it is summary and needs detailing, or it is ambiguous and requires its direction to be determined, or it is open to more than one sense, so that what is meant by it needs a preference that is obtained only by its explication and clarification. The explication occurs in speech in various ways: sometimes it comes after a condition or after something containing the sense of a condition, and at other times after a preposition and its genitive noun, as in this verse. Sound explication has come in it announcing the coming of hope after despair, relief after hardship and joy after sorrow, so that it might fall more sweetly upon hearts.
2- Attributing a thing to the whole while meaning the part: in His saying «وما بث فيهما من دابة» a thing is attributed to the whole of what is mentioned while what is meant is part of it, like the saying of Allah the Exalted «يخرج منهما اللؤلؤ والمرجان», whereas they come out only from the salt [water]. The restriction of creatures to the earth has occurred in another place; Allah the Exalted said: «إن في خلق السموات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار», then said: «وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء فأحيا به الأرض بعد موتها وبث فيها من كل دابة», so He restricted this matter to the earth.

* Benefits:
1- Many discussions of (لو) have preceded in this book. In His saying «ولو بسط الله الرزق لعباده لبغوا في الأرض» a question arises: transgression actually occurs, so how is it valid for it to be negated by what the (لو) of impossibility (lū al-imtināʿiyya) entails? The answer is that what is meant by the negation is all people, just as the negated antecedent was also made the extension [of provision] to all, by the evidence of the wāw [Translator's note: i.e. the plural wāw in (بغوا)], which entails plurality absolutely. Al-Zamakhsharī raised another question and answered it; below is the text of the question and the answer:
"If you say: We see people transgressing against one another, some of them having [provision] extended to them and some having it withheld from them. If those to whom it is extended transgress, why was it extended to them? And if those from whom it is withheld transgress, then transgression can occur without extension, so why make it its condition? I say: There is no doubt that transgression is less with poverty and more and more prevalent with extension, and each of the two is an evident cause of advancing upon transgression or holding back from it. So if extension were general, transgression would prevail, until matters were turned into the reverse of what they are now."
2- Does (إذا) enter upon the imperfect? It is permissible for (إذا) to enter upon the imperfect just as it enters upon the past. Allah the Exalted said: «والليل إذا يغشى», and from it is (إذا يشاء), and the poet's saying:
وإذا ما أشاء أبعث منها ... آخر الليل ناشطا مذعورا
(And whenever I wish, I rouse from her, at the end of the night, a startled wild bull.)
That is because (إذا) is an adverb for the future; so if it enters upon the past [verb] it is future, and upon the imperfect it is explicit in futurity. It is clear that the poet abstracted from the she-camel another thing because of the intensity of her travelling, and for that reason he said (منها) ("from her"). The basic meaning is "I rouse her [Translator's note: the source prints «أبعثهما», "the two of them"] at the end of the night like the nāshiṭ", which is the wild bull going out from one land to another; and al-madhʿūr is the frightened one. It is an allusion (kināya) to one who travels very fast.

dervis-irab:32-35.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْجَوارِ): the ships. It is written without the yāʾ because it is one of the "additional yāʾs" (yāʾāt al-zawāʾid); in pronunciation it is both kept and dropped, in both continuous reading and pause, and it has been read in all these ways. Abū Ḥayyān said: "It is the plural of jāriya, which is an adjective that has come to be treated as a noun, and so has followed governing words." Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī said: If you say: When an adjective is not specific to the things it qualifies, omitting the qualified noun is prohibited — you do not say "I passed by a walking [one]", because walking is general, while you say "I passed by an engineer and a writer" — and running is not one of the attributes specific to the qualified noun, namely ships, so its omission is not permissible; the answer is that the prohibition applies when the adjective has not come to be treated like underived nouns through the prevalence of the noun-character over it, like al-abṭaḥ (the broad watercourse) and al-abraq (the rough mixed ground); otherwise omitting the qualified noun is permissible.
(الأعلام): the mountains, plural of ʿalam. Al-Khansāʾ said:
وإن صخرا لتأتم الهداة به ... كأنه علم في رأسه نار
(Truly Ṣakhr is followed by the guides as though he were a mountain with a fire on its summit.)
This is one of its many meanings.
(رَواكِدَ): fixed, not moving. One says rakada al-māʾu rukūdan, of the pattern qaʿada: it became still; likewise the wind, the ship, and the sun when the height of noon stands still. Everything fixed in a place is rākid. Rakada al-mīzān: the balance became level; rakada al-qawm: the people became quiet.
(يُوبِقْهُنَّ): He destroys them. One says wabaqa, yabiqu, like waʿada, yaʿidu; and wabiqa, yabqu [Translator's note: so in the source], of the pattern taʿiba, yatʿabu, wabqan with sukūn on the bāʾ; and wabiqa, yawbaqu, wabaqan with fatḥa on the bāʾ, wubūqan and mawbiqan; and istawbaqa: he perished, so he is wabiq. Awbaqahu ībāqan: he destroyed him, abased him and detained him.

* I'rab:
(وَمِنْ آياتِهِ الْجَوارِ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلامِ): (من آياته) is a fronted khabar (predicate); (الجوار) is a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), the sign of its nominative case being the ḍamma implied (muqaddara) on the yāʾ that is omitted in writing and pronunciation, or in writing only; (في البحر) is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and (كالأعلام) is also a ḥāl. It was mentioned in the vocabulary section that the noun-character has prevailed over (الجوار). The wording of Abū al-Baqāʾ: "(الجوار) is a mubtadaʾ, or a fāʿil (agent) made nominative by the preposition [phrase]; (في البحر) is a ḥāl from it, its governor being the [notion of] being established; and it may be attached to (الجوار). (كالأعلام), on the first aspect, is a second ḥāl, and on the second aspect it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in (الجوار)." (إِنْ يَشَأْ يُسْكِنِ الرِّيحَ فَيَظْلَلْنَ رَواكِدَ عَلى ظَهْرِهِ): (إن) is conditional; (يشأ) is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), its fāʿil optionally latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He", referring back to Allah the Exalted; (يسكن) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (الريح) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is conjunctive; (يظللن) is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is joined to the nūn of the feminine plural, in the position of jussive (majzūm), conjoined to (يسكن الريح); it has fatḥa on the lām because the past has kasra — you say ẓaliltu qāʾiman (I remained standing). The nūn of the feminine plural is the noun of (يظللن), because it is a defective (nāqiṣ) verb, and (رواكد) is its khabar; and (على ظهره) is attached to (رواكد). (إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ): (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (آيات) is the noun of (إن); (لكل) is a naʿt (adjective) of (آيات); (صبار) is a muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of a genitive construct); and (شكور) is a naʿt of (صبار). (أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ بِما كَسَبُوا وَيَعْفُ عَنْ كَثِيرٍ): (أو) is a conjunction; (يوبقهن) [Translator's note: the source prints «ويوقهن», a misprint] is conjoined to (يسكن), i.e. He scatters them [Translator's note: the source prints «يفرقهنّ», "He scatters them"; al-Kashshāf's wording, quoted next, suggests «يغرقهنّ», "He drowns them"] by the storming of the wind upon them. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: To what is (يوبقهن) conjoined? I say: To (يسكن), because the meaning is: If He wills, He stills the wind and they become motionless, or He makes it storm and they are scattered [Translator's note: again «فيفرقن» in the source; «فيغرقن», 'they are drowned', appears in al-Kashshāf] by its storming" — or by a fault befalling their equipment. (بما) is attached to (يوبقهن); (ما) may be relative or maṣdariyya (infinitival), and the bāʾ is causal, i.e. because of the sins they earned. (يعف) is also conjoined to (يسكن), and the meaning is: or, if He wills, He destroys some people and saves others by way of pardoning them; and (عن كثير) is attached to (يعف). (وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ فِي آياتِنا ما لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ): the wāw is a conjunction, and (يعلم) is conjoined to an implied cause, i.e. "He scatters them in order to take vengeance on them, and so that those who dispute may know" — thus al-Zamakhsharī and al-Jalāl al-Suyūṭī implied it. Abū Ḥayyān rejected it, saying: "Implying 'in order to take vengeance on them' is far-fetched, because what results from the condition is the destruction of some people and the saving of others, so it is not good to imply as the cause [only] one of the two matters." Al-Karkhī followed up on him, saying in reply to him and in defence of al-Suyūṭī's i'rab: "Rather, it is good to imply 'in order to take vengeance on them', as our shaykh said, because what is intended is to give the cause of the destruction only, which al-Suyūṭī implied with his words 'He scatters them', since that is what suits the conjoined cause, namely (ويعلم)." Al-Zamakhsharī defended the first i'rab, namely conjunction to the omitted cause, by saying: "The like of it, in conjunction to an omitted cause, is not rare in the Qur'an; from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted «ولنجعله آية للناس», and His saying «وخلق الله السموات والأرض بالحق ولتجزى كل نفس بما كسبت»." As for al-Zajjāj, he parsed it as accusative by an implied (أن), and Abū al-Baqāʾ followed him; he said: because before it there is a requital (jazāʾ); you say "Whatever you do I will do the like of it, wa-ukrimaka (and honour you)" with the accusative; or if you wish "wa-ukrimuka" with the nominative, on [the sense of] "and I honour you"; or if you wish "wa-ukrimka" with the jussive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In this i'rab there is room for consideration, because Sībawayh said in his Book: 'Know that the accusative with the fāʾ and the wāw in one's saying "If you come to me I will come to you wa-uʿṭiyaka (and give you)" is weak; it is akin to his saying «وألحق بالحجاز فاستريحا» (and I will join the Ḥijāz and so find rest). This is permissible but is not the norm of speech nor its proper way, except that in the requital it has become a little stronger, because it is not necessary that he does [it] unless there is an action from the first [party]; so since it resembled what does not make it necessary, like the interrogative and the like, they permitted this in it despite its weakness.'" Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not permissible to construe the widespread reading on a weak aspect which is not the norm of speech nor its proper way; had it been of this category, Sībawayh would not have left his Book without it, for he mentioned its parallels among the difficult verses." [Translator's note: the source attributes both statements to al-Zamakhsharī; the same discussion is found in al-Kashshāf.] Furthermore, (ويعلم) has been read with the nominative, as resumptive, on the basis that it is a nominal or a verbal clause. On its being nominal, the relative noun is a mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun referring back to an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "and He knows those who responded" [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has (الذين يجادلون), "those who dispute"]; on its being verbal, the relative noun is the fāʿil. It has also been read in the jussive, by conjunction to the preceding apodosis, as though He said: "If He wills, He combines three matters: the destruction of some people, the saving of others and the warning of others." (الذين) is a fāʿil or a mafʿūl bihi, as has preceded; the clause (يجادلون) is the ṣila (relative clause); (في آياتنا) is attached to (يجادلون); (ما) is negating, or the Ḥijāzī negating (mā); (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (محيص) is genitive (majrūr) in form and nominative (marfūʿ) in position as a mubtadaʾ,
or as the noun of (ما); and the negative clause takes the place of the two objects of (يعلم), which is suspended (muʿallaq) from operation by the negation.

* Rhetoric:
The wind between singular and plural: It has been mentioned in another place in this book that "wind" (al-rīḥ) has not occurred in the singular in the Qur'an except for punishment. Someone has tried to breach this generalization, saying that the saying of Allah the Exalted «إن يشأ يسكن الريح فيظللن رواكد على ظهره» breaches it, because the wind mentioned is a blessing. I say: This is a mistaken understanding; on the contrary, it confirms the application of this rule in its generality, because He prefaced it with conditional (إن), which conveys that the default for the singular wind is punishment, and that when He wishes to take it out of its general sense He restricts it with conditional (إن); so that when that is done, He refers the pronoun back to it in the plural, saying (فيظللن رواكد), i.e. the winds [Translator's note: so in the source; the pronoun in (فيظللن) is usually taken to refer to the ships]. The noble ḥadīth has supported the generalization we have adopted, for he said: "O Allah, make it winds (riyāḥ) and do not make it a wind (rīḥ)."

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿عۤسۤقۤ﴾.
It is reported of Ibn ʿAbbās that he used to say: حم سق, without putting an ʿayn in it, and he would say: the sīn is every sect (firqa) that will be, and the qāf is every community (jamāʿa) that will be.
Al-Farrāʾ said: [And] I saw it in some of the codices of (ʿAbd Allāh) as "حم سق", just as Ibn ʿAbbās said.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُوحِيۤ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾.
﴿حم عسق﴾: it is said that they were revealed to every prophet, just as they were revealed to Muḥammad, Allah bless him.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: and by them ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib used to know the trials (fitan). Some have read: "كذلك يوحَى", passive, its agent not named; then you put الله العزيز الحكيم in the nominative, referring the verb to Him. Just as Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: "وَكَذلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ منَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلُ أَوْلادِهِمْ" then said: (شركاؤهم), i.e. their partners made it seem fair to them. Likewise the saying of whoever read: "يُسَبَّحُ له فيها بالغُدُوِّ والآصالِ" and then you say: (رجالٌ), putting it in the nominative, meaning: men glorify Him.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿لِّتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾: Umm al-Qurā (the Mother of Towns) is Mecca, and "those around it" are the Arabs; ﴿وَتُنذِرَ يَوْمَ ٱلْجَمْعِ﴾: its meaning is: and that you warn them of the Day of Gathering. Like it is His saying: ﴿إنَّمَا ذَلِكُمُ الشّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ أَولياءَهُ﴾; its meaning is: he makes you fear his allies.
His saying: ﴿فَرِيقٌ فِي ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيقٌ فِي ٱلسَّعِيرِ﴾.
Nominative by resumption (istiʾnāf), as in your saying: "I saw the people: wretched and happy (شقى وسعيد)"; and had it been فريقاً فى الجنة وفريقا فى السعير (accusative), it would have been correct, but the nominative is better in Arabic.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجاً وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ أَزْواجاً﴾.
He says: He made for every thing among the livestock a mate, so that they may multiply and you may multiply.
His saying: ﴿يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ﴾: the meaning of فيه is: by it (به), and Allah knows best.

farraa:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿فَلِذَلِكَ فَٱدْعُ وَٱسْتَقِمْ﴾, i.e. "so for this Qurʾān"; and the like of it is frequent in the Qurʾān, and we have mentioned it: هذا in the place of ذلك, and ذلك in the place of هذا. And the meaning is: "so to that (فإلى ذلك) call", just as you say [167/b]: "I called to (إلى) so-and-so" and "I called for (لـ) so-and-so".

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾.
It is reported that the Anṣār collected for the Prophet, Allah bless him, a sum to spend, to help him with what befell him concerning his Companions. They brought it to the Prophet, Allah bless him, and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has guided us through you, and you are the son of our sister, so seek help with this sum for what befalls you." He did not accept it, and Allah sent down concerning that: Say to them: I do not ask you for any wage for the message except affection for my kinship with you.
And Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿لاَّ أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْراً إِلاَّ ٱلْمَوَدَّةَ فِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾: in my kinship with Quraysh.
«[Translator's note: the source has «أجراً إلى المودة» in the paraphrase, where إلا is evidently meant; translated as "except".]»

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَمْحُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْبَاطِلَ﴾.
It is not referred back to ﴿يختم﴾ so as to be jussive (majzūm); it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf), in the position of the nominative, even though there is no wāw in it in the written text. Like it, among what has had the wāw dropped while it is in the position of the nominative, is His saying: ﴿وَيَدْعُ الإنْسَانُ بِالشَّرِّ﴾ and His saying: ﴿سَنَدْعُ الزَّبَانِيَةَ﴾.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾. He mentioned the servants, then said: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾ as though He addressed them; and the generality (al-ʿawāmm) read it with yāʾ.
Al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to me, from a man whom he named, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from his father, who said: I recited at night: ﴿ويعلم ما تفعلون﴾ and did not know whether to say يفعلون or تفعلون. So I went in the morning to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd to ask him about that. A man came to him and said: "O Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, a man had an affair with a woman in his youth, then they separated and repented; is it lawful for him to marry her?" He said: ʿAbd Allāh said, raising his voice: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقْبَلُ ٱلتَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ وَيَعْفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّئَاتِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: and so did ʿAlqama ibn Qays, Ibrāhīm and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it; and it is reported of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī that he read it likewise, with tāʾ.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ [وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ] ﴾.
الذين may be in the position of the accusative, meaning: "and Allah answers those who believed"; and it has come in the Revelation: ﴿فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾, and the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: "so their Lord answered them (فأجابهم)"; except that when you say استجاب you bring lām in on the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and when you say أجاب you drop the lām. So استجابهم is in the meaning of استجاب لهم, as He said: ﴿وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ﴾, the meaning, and Allah knows best, being: "and when they measure for them or weigh for them, they cause loss". And الذين may be in the position of the nominative, making the verb theirs, i.e.: those who believed respond to Allah, and Allah increases them, beyond their response and their assent, out of His bounty.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿خَلْقُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَمَا بَثَّ فِيهِمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ﴾.
He meant: what He spread in the earth, not the heaven; so it came in the exegesis. Like it, among what is put in the dual while its meaning is one, is His saying: ﴿يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُما الُّلؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجَانُ﴾, while it comes out only from the salt water, not the fresh.

farraa:34-34.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَعْفُ عَن كَثِيرٍ﴾: and ويعلَمَ الذين is referred back to the jussive, except that it has been diverted (ṣurifa); and the jussive, when what is conjoined to it is diverted from it, becomes accusative, as in the poet's saying:
فإن يهلِك أبو قابوسَ يَهلِك * ربيعُ الناسِ والبلدُ الحرامُ ونُمسكَ بعده بذناب عَيْسٍ * أجبِّ الظهرِ ليس له سَنام
(If Abū Qābūs perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred land perish, and we shall hold on after him to the tail of a life [like a camel] with a cut-down back, having no hump.)
And the nominative is permissible in what is accusative by diversion (ṣarf).

farraa:35-35.t: And some people read it so, putting it in the nominative: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ﴾. Like it, among what is resumed and made nominative, is His saying: ﴿ثم يتوبُ اللّهُ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِك على من يشاء﴾ in Barāʾa; and had someone put ويعلمُ in the jussive, he would have been right.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كبير ٱلإِثْمِ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it "كبير"; and it is explained from Ibn ʿAbbās that the great one of sin is shirk (associating partners with Allah). So this agrees with whoever read كبير [الإثم] in the singular. The generality read: ﴿كَبَائِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَٱلْفَوَاحِشَ﴾, making كبائر as though it were something general, while in origin it is one. And I would prefer, for whoever reads كبائر, that he put الفواحش in the genitive.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْبَغْيُ هُمْ يَنتَصِرُونَ﴾.
It was revealed specifically about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah have mercy on him). That was because a man of the Anṣār attacked him in the presence of the Messenger of Allah and reviled him, and Abū Bakr did not answer him back, and the Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him, did not forbid the Anṣārī. Then Abū Bakr turned to him and answered him back, and the Prophet, Allah bless him, rose as though angry. Abū Bakr followed him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what you did to me is harder on me than what he did to me: he reviled me and you did not forbid him, and I answered him back and you rose as though angry." The Prophet, Allah bless him, said: "The angel was answering him on your behalf while you were silent; when you answered him, the angel went back, so I sprang up with him." Then this verse was revealed. And Sharīk explained it, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrāhīm, regarding His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَابَهُمُ ٱلْبَغْيُ هُمْ يَنتَصِرُونَ﴾: they said: they used to dislike abasing themselves before the wicked, lest these be emboldened against them.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَمَنِ ٱنتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن سَبِيلٍ﴾.
It was also revealed about Abū Bakr.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ﴾.
Some said: they hide it because of the humiliation that is upon them; and some said: they looked at the Fire with their hearts and did not see it with their eyes, because they are gathered blind.

farraa:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ﴾.
Before them He mentioned الإنسان (man) in the singular; and الإنسان may be one and may be in the meaning of a plural, so He returned the hāʾ and mīm (هم) to it according to the interpretation. Like it is His saying: ﴿وَخُلِقَ الإنْسَانُ ضَعِيفاً﴾, by which all people are meant; and for that reason exception (istithnāʾ) is allowed with it while it is singular in wording, as in the saying of Allah: ﴿إنَّ الإنسانَ لَفِى خُسْرٍ إلا الذين آمنوا﴾. Like it also: ﴿وَكَمْ مِّنْ مَلَكٍ فِى السّماواتِ﴾, then He said: ﴿لاَ تُغْنِى شَفَاعَتُهُمْ﴾, though He mentioned only "an angel", because it is in the interpretation of a plural.

farraa:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَاثاً﴾.
Purely, with no males among them; and He grants to whom He wills males purely, with no females among them; or He pairs them (يزوجهم): he says: He makes some of them sons and some of them daughters; that is the "pairing" in this place. The Arabs say: "He has sons shiṭra (half and half)" when half of them are males and half females; and the meaning of this, and Allah knows best, is like the meaning of what is in the Book of Allah.

farraa:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلاَّ وَحْياً﴾.
As the Prophet, Allah bless him, used to see in his sleep, and He would inspire him; or from behind a veil, as He spoke to Moses from behind a veil; or He sends a messenger, an angel [of His angels], who reveals by His permission, and speaks to the Prophet whatever Allah wills. [And that is in His saying: "أو يرسلَُ رسولا ... (51)": the nominative and the accusative; [it is] better. Al-Farrāʾ said: Nāfiʿ of Medina read it in the nominative, and the generality read it in the accusative.] And whoever puts "يرسل" in the nominative says "فيوحى" with the yāʾ jussive (vowelless).
«[Translator's note: the bracketed phrase «الرفع والنصب أجود» is unclear as transmitted; translated literally.]»

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِي مَا ٱلْكِتَابُ وَلاَ ٱلإِيمَانُ وَلَـٰكِن جَعَلْنَاهُ نُوراً﴾.
He means the Revelation (al-tanzīl). Some said: He meant the Qurʾān and faith; and it is allowed to say جعلناه (singular pronoun) for two, because the action (fiʿl), in the multiplicity of its names, is held together by "the action". Do you not see that you say: "Your coming and your going grieves (يغمنى) me", and they are two? So this is of that kind.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (كذلك يوحي إليك) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e.: He reveals to you a revelation like that revelation; the preposition phrase «من قبلك» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); «العزيز الحكيم» are two adjectives.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «له ما في السماوات» is resumptive; the clause «وهو العلي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive one; «العظيم» is a second khabar (predicate).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition phrase «بحمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «يسبِّحون»; «ألا» is for drawing attention; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The preposition phrase «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted second object; the clause «الله حفيظ» is a khabar (predicate); and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of «ما» that operates like laysa.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The wāw is resumptive; the kāf is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the genitive maṣdar «لتنذر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أوحينا»; the clause «لا ريب فيه» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «يوم الجمع»; «فريق» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is what «في الجنة» is attached to; beginning with an indefinite is permitted because the context is one of detailing; and «فريق في السعير» is like its counterpart.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the clause «ولكن يدخل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ولو شاء الله»; the preposition phrase «في رحمته» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يدخل»; the clause «والظالمون ما لهم ...» is resumptive; the clause «ما لهم من ولي» is a khabar (predicate); «ولي» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one, and the clause after it is resumptive; the preposition phrase «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object; the clause «فالله هو الولي» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: if they want true protectors, then Allah ...; the clause «وهو يحيي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «الله.. الولي»; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position; and the preposition phrase «على كل» is attached to «قدير».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The wāw is resumptive; «ما» is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause «اختلفتم» is the khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «من شيء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ما»; His saying «ذلكم الله ربي» is a mubtadaʾ and its two khabars; and the clause «عليه توكلت» is a third khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: «فاطر» is a fourth khabar (predicate); the clause «جعل» is a fifth khabar; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) second object; the preposition phrase «من أنفسكم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أزواجا». His saying «ومن الأنعام»: the wāw is conjunctive, and the preposition phrase is attached to a ḥāl of «أزواجا»; the implied «لها» is attached to the implied second object; and the second «أزواجا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first, the implied form being: and of the livestock, for them, mates. The clause «يذرؤكم» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of «جعل»; the preposition phrase «فيه» is attached to «يذرؤكم»; the clause «ليس كمثله شيء» is a sixth khabar; the kāf is redundant (zāʾida), «مثله» is the khabar of laysa, and «شيء» is its noun; and the clause «وهو السميع» is conjoined to the clause «ليس كمثله شيء».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The clause «له مقاليد» is a seventh khabar (predicate), and likewise the clause «يبسط»; the clause «إنه بكل شيء عليم» is resumptive; and the preposition phrase «بكل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».
