The clause «ما كنت تدري ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the pronoun in (إليك).
The clause «تدري ...» is in the position of accusative as khabar of كنت.
The clause «ما الكتاب ...» is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of تدري, which is suspended (muʿallaq) from governing by the interrogative ما.
The clause «جعلناه ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause ما كنت تدري.
The clause «نهدي ...» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (نورا).
The clause «نشاء ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إنّك لتهدي ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تهدي ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of إنّ.
53- (صراط) badal (substitute) of the first صراط, a definite badal of an indefinite, genitive like it. (الذي) relative noun, in the position of genitive as a naʿt of the Name of Majesty. (له) attached to a fronted khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (ما). (في السموات) attached to an omitted ṣila of ما. The second (ما) is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the first (ما). (في الأرض) the ṣila of the second ما. (ألا) for drawing attention (tanbīh). (إلى الله) attached to (تصير).
The clause «له ما في السموات ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «تصير الأمور» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ يوحي}: The readers read «يُوْحي» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, active, the agent being Allah the Exalted; «والعزيزُ الحكيمُ» are two naʿts (adjectives). The kāf is in the position of the accusative, either as an adjective of a maṣdar (verbal noun) or as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from its pronoun, i.e. "He reveals a revealing like that revealing." Ibn Kathīr read — and it is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr — «يُوْحَى» with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, passive. There are three aspects regarding what stands in place of the agent. First: a latent pronoun referring to «كذلك», because it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the implied form being: "the like of that revealing — it is revealed to you"; so «مثلُ ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «يُوْحى هو إليك» is its khabar (predicate). Second: what stands in place of the agent is «إليك», and the kāf is in the position of the accusative on the two preceding aspects. Third: what stands [in its place] is the clause «اللَّهُ العزيزُ», i.e. "this wording is revealed to you." The principles of the Basrans do not support this, because a clause is neither an agent nor stands in its place.
Abū Ḥaywa, al-Aʿmash and Abān read «نُوْحي» with the nūn, and it agrees with [the reading of] the majority. It is possible that the clause «اللَّهُ العزيزُ» is in the position of the accusative as the object of «نُوْحي», i.e. "We reveal to you this wording," except that this involves quoting clauses without an explicit verb of saying. «نُوْحي», with its different readings, may be in its proper sense of present or future, so that His saying {وَإِلَى الذين مِن قَبْلِكَ} is attached to an omitted [verb], since that [attachment to it] is impossible, its implied form being "and He revealed to those ..."; or it may be in the sense of the past, brought in the form of the imperfect for a purpose, namely depicting the situation.
His saying: «اللَّهُ العزيزُ»: It may be nominative as the agent in the reading of the majority; it may be nominative by an implied verb in the reading of Ibn Kathīr, as if it were said "who reveals it?" and it was said "Allah," as in {يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بالغدو والآصال} [al-Nūr: 36] and the saying:
3964 - لِيُبْكَ يزيدُ ضارِعٌ. . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [by] one humbled …)
which has passed; it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ with what follows as its khabar, the clause standing in place of the agent as has passed; and «العزيزُ الحكيمُ» may be two predicates or two adjectives. The clause {لَهُ مَا فِي السماوات} is a first or second predicate according to what preceded regarding «العزيزُ الحكيمُ».
Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed «العزيز» to be a mubtadaʾ with «الحكيمُ» its khabar, or its adjective, and {لَهُ مَا فِي السماوات} its khabar. This is questionable, since the apparent sense is that both follow the Divine Name; and when you say «جاء زيدٌ العاقلُ الفاضلُ» ("Zayd, the intelligent, the virtuous, came"), you do not make «العاقل» nominative as a mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {تَكَادُ السماوات يَتَفَطَّرْنَ}: The disagreement and the discussion of it have passed in full in Maryam, except that al-Zamakhsharī added here: "There is transmitted from Yūnus from Abū ʿAmr an unusual reading, «تَتَفَطَّرْنَ», with two tāʾs together with the nūn; its parallel is a rare form transmitted in the Nawādir of Ibn al-Aʿrābī: «الإِبلُ تَتَشَمَّمْن» ('the camels are sniffing')." The Shaykh said: "The apparent case is that this is an error on his part, because Ibn Khālawayh said in Shādhdh al-Qirāʾāt, verbatim: '«تَنْفَطِرْنَ» with the tāʾ and the nūn: Yūnus from Abū ʿAmr.' Ibn Khālawayh said: 'This is a rare form, because the Arabs do not combine two markers of the feminine; one does not say «النساءُ تَقُمْنَ» but «يَقُمْنَ», {والوالدات يُرْضِعْنَ} [al-Baqara: 233], and one does not say «تُرْضَعْنَ». Abū ʿUmar al-Zāhid had transmitted in the Nawādir of Ibn al-Aʿrābī «الإِبلُ تَتشمَّمْن», and we rejected it; now this has strengthened it.'" The Shaykh said: "If the copies of al-Zamakhsharī agree on his saying 'with two tāʾs together with the nūn,' it is an error; if in some of them it is 'with a tāʾ together with the nūn,' it agrees with the statement of Ibn Khālawayh, and 'with two tāʾs' is a corruption by the copyists. Likewise their writing «تَتَفَطَّرْن» and «تَتَشَمَّمْنَ» with two tāʾs" — end of quote.
I say: how can it be right that their writing «تَتَشَمَّمْن» with two tāʾs is an error? That is because Ibn Khālawayh cited it in the context of rarity and rejection, until it was strengthened for him by this reading; and it is only rare and rejected with two tāʾs, for then it is an imperfect attributed to the pronoun of the camels, so its imperfect prefix ought to have been a yāʾ dotted below, as in «النساءُ يَقُمْنَ»; so it ought to have been said «الإِبلُ يَتَشَمَّمْنَ», with the lower-dotted yāʾ then the upper-dotted tāʾ. When it came with two tāʾs, both dotted above, its rarity and objectionableness became apparent. Had it been as the Shaykh said — that their writing it with two tāʾs is an error and it ought to be written with one tāʾ — there would be nothing anomalous or objectionable in it, because it would be parallel to «النسوةُ قد خَرَجْنَ» ("the women have gone out"), which is a past verb attributed to the pronoun of feminines; likewise, had it been written with a lower yāʾ and an upper tāʾ, there would be nothing anomalous or objectionable in it. Anomaly and objection arise only when it is with two tāʾs dotted above. Moreover, whether «تَتَفَطَّرْنَ» is read with two tāʾs or with a tāʾ and a nūn, it is rare, as Ibn Khālawayh mentioned; and this reading was not read in its counterpart in Sūrat Maryam.
His saying: «مِنْ فَوْقِهِنَّ»: There are three aspects regarding this pronoun. First: it refers to the heavens, i.e. their splitting begins from this direction, so «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent, attached to what precedes it. Second: it [refers] to the earths, because the earth was mentioned before that. Third: it refers to the factions of the disbelievers and the heretical groups — so said al-Akhfash the Younger. Makkī rejected it and said: "That is not permissible for the males of the children of Adam." This does not bind al-Akhfash, for he said "the factions and the groups," so he observed that meaning.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً}: There are two aspects in it. The more apparent: it is the object of «أَوْحَيْنا», and the kāf is for the maṣdar (verbal noun), as an adjective or a ḥāl (circumstantial). Second: it is a ḥāl from the kāf, and the kāf is the object of «أَوْحَيْنا», i.e. "We revealed the like of that revealing, being an Arabic Qurʾān." Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this, and the kāf being a noun in prose is the doctrine of al-Akhfash.
His saying: «ومَنْ حَوْلها»: conjoined to «أهل», implied before «أمَّ القرى», i.e. "that you may warn the people of the Mother of Cities and those around it." The second object is omitted, i.e. "the punishment." It has been read «لِيُنْذِرَ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. the Qurʾān [is the agent]. His saying {وَتُنذِرَ يَوْمَ الجمع} is the second object, and the first is omitted, i.e. "and you may warn people of the punishment of the Day of Gathering"; so He omitted the first object from the second warning, just as He omitted the second object from the first warning.
His saying: {لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ}: a statement, so it is resumptive. It may be a ḥāl from «يومَ الجمع». Al-Zamakhsharī made it parenthetical, and that is not apparent technically, since it does not occur between two mutually dependent elements.
His saying: «فَرِيقٌ»: The majority read it in the nominative on one of two aspects. Either as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the prepositional phrase after it as its khabar (predicate); this was acceptable for an indefinite noun because it is a context of detailing, as in the saying:
3965 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فثوبٌ لَبِسْتُ وثَوْبٌ أَجُرّْ
(… one garment I wore, and one garment I trail.)
Or the khabar may be implied, its implied form being "of them is a party"; beginning with an indefinite noun was acceptable for two things: its predicate being fronted as a prepositional phrase, and its being described by the prepositional phrase after it. The second: it is the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. "they," meaning those gathered, indicated by His saying «يومَ الجَمْعِ».
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «فريقاً، وفريقاً» in the accusative as a ḥāl from an omitted clause, i.e. "they split up," meaning those gathered. Makkī said: "Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative of «فريقاً» in [ordinary] speech, in the sense of: you warn a party [who will be] in Paradise and a party in the Blaze of the Day of Gathering." I say: it has preceded that Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it so; it seems he [Makkī] was not aware that it is a reading; indeed the apparent sense of his transmission from these two imams is that they were not aware of it. He made «فريقاً» a first object of «تُنْذِرَ» and «يومَ الجَمْعِ» a second object. On its face there is a difficulty, namely that the warning does not befall the two parties while they are in Paradise and in the Blaze; the warning is only before they settle in them. It can be answered that what is meant is whoever is of the people of Paradise and of the people of the Blaze, even if not in them at the time of the warning. «في الجنة» is an adjective of «فَريقاً» or attached to that omitted [verb].

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {أَمِ اتخذوا}: This is the disjunctive «أم» (al-munqaṭiʿa), construed as «بل» of transition together with the hamza of disapproval, or as the hamza alone, or as «بل» alone.
His saying: {فالله هُوَ الولي}: The fāʾ conjoins what follows it to what precedes it. Al-Zamakhsharī made it the apodosis (jawāb) of an implied condition, as if it were said: "If they want true protectors, then Allah is the Protector."

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {فَاطِرُ}: The majority read it in the nominative, as the khabar (predicate) of «ذلكم», or as a naʿt (adjective) of «ربِّي» on the basis that its annexation is pure [i.e. definite]; on this «عليه توكَّلْتُ» is parenthetical. Or it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is «جَعَلَ لكم», or the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. "He." Zayd ibn ʿAlī [read] «فاطرِ» in the genitive as an adjective of the Divine Name in His saying «إلى اللَّهِ», with what is between them parenthetical, or as a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ in «عليه» or «إليه».
Makkī said: "Al-Kisāʾī permitted the accusative as a vocative." Others said: by way of praise. "The genitive is permissible in [ordinary] speech as a substitute for the hāʾ in «عليه»." I say: Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the genitive. As for its accusative, I do not know it as a reading.
His saying: «يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فيه»: «في» may be in its proper sense, the meaning being: He multiplies you in this arrangement, namely that He made for people and cattle mates, so that procreation occurred between their males and females. The pronoun in «يَذرَؤُكم» is for those addressed and the cattle, giving precedence to the rational over the others, who are absent (third person). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is among the rules with two causes." The Shaykh said: "It is a strange term; he means that the second person prevails over the third person when they are combined." Then al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what is the meaning of 'He multiplies you in this arrangement,' and why was it not said 'He multiplies you by it'? I say: this arrangement was made as the source and mine of spreading and multiplying. Do you not see that you say: for animals, in the creation of mates there is multiplication, as Allah the Exalted said: {وَلَكُمْ فِي القصاص حَيَاةٌ} [al-Baqara: 179]?" The second [aspect]: it is causal, like the bāʾ, i.e. He multiplies you by means of it. The pronoun refers to the making or to what is created.
His saying: {لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ}: There are several aspects regarding this verse. First — and it is the well-known one among the grammarians — the kāf is redundant (zāʾida) in the predicate of «ليس», and «شيءٌ» is its noun, the implied form being "nothing is like Him." They said: were it not for claiming its redundancy, it would follow that He has a like, which is impossible; for, on the kāf being original, the implied form would be "there is nothing like the like of Him," so it negates likeness to His like, thereby affirming that He has a like, which like has no like; and that is impossible — Allah is exalted above that.
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "Were it not redundant, that would lead to the impossible, since the meaning would be that He has a like and His like has no like. In that there is a contradiction, because if He has a like, then His like has a like, namely Him; besides which affirming a like for Allah the Exalted is impossible." I say: this is an unusual way of establishing the redundancy, and it is a fine way with fine craftsmanship.
Second: «مثل» is the redundant one, as it is redundant in His saying, Exalted is He: {بِمِثْلِ مَآ آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ} [al-Baqara: 137]. Al-Ṭabarī said: "Just as the kāf was added in the saying:
3966 - وصَالياتٍ كَكَما يُؤَثْفَيْنْ ...
(And fire-blackened [hearthstones], like as they are set up as trivets …)
and the other's saying:
3967 - فصُيِّروا مثلَ كعَصْفٍ مَأْكُوْلْ ...
(And they were made like [as] eaten straw …)"
This is not good, because the addition of nouns is not permissible; moreover the implied form would become "there is nothing like Him (ka-huwa)," and the entry of the kāf onto pronouns is not permissible except in poetry.
Third: the Arabs say «مثلُكَ لا يَفْعَلُ كذا» ("one like you does not do such"), meaning the addressee himself, because they want to exaggerate in negating the quality from the addressee, so they negate it in wording from his like, and thus its negation from him is established by implication. From this is the poet's saying:
3968 - على مِثْلِ ليلى يَقْتُل المرءُ نفسَه ... وإنْ باتَ مِنْ ليلى على اليأس طاويا
(For one like Laylā a man kills himself, even if he spends the night despairing of Laylā, hungry.)
Aws ibn Ḥajar said:
3969 - ليس كمثلِ الفتى زُهَيْرٍ ... خَلْقٌ يُوازِيه في الفضائلِ
(There is none like the youth Zuhayr — no creature that equals him in virtues.)
Another said:
3970 - سَعْدُ بنُ زيدٍ إذا أبصرْتَ فضلَهُمُ ... فما كمِثْلِهِمْ في الناسِ مِنْ أَحَدِ
(Saʿd ibn Zayd — when you behold their excellence, there is no one among people like them.)
Ibn Qutayba said: "The Arabs put «المِثْل» in place of the self, saying «مثلي لا يُقال له هذا» ('one like me is not told this'), i.e. I am not told." It has been said: [a parallel to] attributing a like to one who has no like is your saying "so-and-so's hand is outstretched," meaning that he is generous, without regard in reality to the hand, so that you say it of one who has no hand, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ} [al-Māʾida: 64].
Fourth: what is meant by «المِثْل» is the attribute; that is because «المِثْل» is in the sense of «المَثَل», and «المَثَل» is the attribute, as in His saying, Exalted is He: {مَّثَلُ الجنة} [al-Raʿd: 35]. So the meaning would be: nothing among the attributes belonging to others is like His attribute, Exalted is He; and this is an easy construal.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {أَنْ أَقِيمُواْ}: Several aspects are possible in it. First: it is maṣdariyya, in the position of the nominative as the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is: establish," i.e. the prescribed religion is the affirmation of the oneness of Allah the Exalted. Second: it is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for the relative noun, as if it were said: "He has prescribed for you the affirmation of the oneness of Allah the Exalted." Third: it is in the position of the genitive as a substitute for «الدين». Fourth: it is also in the position of the genitive as a substitute for the hāʾ. Fifth: it is explicative (mufassira), because it is preceded by what is in the sense of saying.

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {أُورِثُواْ}: Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «وُرِّثوا» with doubling, [from] «وُرِّثَ», passive.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {فَلِذَلِكَ فادع}: There are two aspects regarding the lām. First: it is in the sense of «إلى» (to). Second: it is causal, i.e. because of the division and disagreement, call to the upright religion.
His saying: «وأُمِرْتُ لأَعْدِلَ»: The implied form may be "and I have been commanded that, in order that I be just." It has been said: "and I have been commanded to be just," so the lām is redundant. This is questionable, because after making the lām redundant you need to imply a preposition, i.e. «بأَنْ أَعْدِلَ».

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {والذين يُحَآجُّونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); «حُجَّتُهم» is a second mubtadaʾ, «داحِضَةٌ» is the khabar (predicate) of the second, and the second with its predicate is the predicate of the first. Makkī parsed «حُجَّتُهم» as a badal (substitute) for the relative noun, a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). The hāʾ in «له» refers to Allah or to the Messenger, peace be upon him, i.e. after people had responded to Allah the Exalted, or after Allah had responded to His Messenger when he invoked against his people.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {لَعَلَّ الساعة قَرِيبٌ}: He made «قَريب» masculine, even though it is an adjective of a feminine, only because «الساعة» is in the sense of the time, or the resurrection; or on the sense of relation, i.e. "possessing nearness"; or by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "the coming of the Hour." It has been said: to distinguish it from nearness of kinship. And it has been said: because its feminine is figurative — Makkī transmitted it — and it amounts to nothing, since «الشمسُ طالعٌ» and «القِدْرُ فائرٌ» are not permissible. The clause of hope or apprehension suspends (taʿlīq) the [verb of] knowing. The like of it has preceded at the end of al-Anbiyāʾ.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {نَزِدْ لَهُ فِي حَرْثِهِ}: It has preceded that the condition being a past verb and the apodosis (jazāʾ) a jussive (majzūm) imperfect is not restricted to occurring with «كان», contrary to Abū al-Ḥakam, the author of Kitāb al-Iʿrāb, who said: "That is not permissible except with «كان», save by poetic necessity." The grammarians allowed it without restriction, and cited the verse of al-Farazdaq:
3971 - دَسَّتْ رسولاً بأنَّ القوم إنْ قَدِرُوا ... عليك يَشْفُوا صدوراً ذاتَ تَوْغيرِ
(She secretly sent a messenger [saying] that the people, if they get power over you, will heal breasts full of rancour.)
and also his saying:
3972 - تَعَشَّ فإنْ عاهَدْتَني لا تَخُونني ... نكنْ مِثْلَ مَنْ يا ذئبُ يصْطَحِبان
(Eat your supper; if you pledge to me not to betray me, we shall be, O wolf, like two who keep company.)
Ibn Miqsam, al-Zaʿfarānī and Maḥbūb read «يَزِدْ» and «يُؤْتِه» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. Allah the Exalted. Sallām read «نُؤْتِهُ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ of the pronoun, which is the original, and it is the dialect of the Ḥijāz. The disagreement of the readers on that has preceded.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {شَرَعُواْ لَهُمْ}: The nominative pronoun may refer to the partners and the genitive one to the disbelievers; the reverse is also possible, because they assigned them shares.
His saying: «وإنَّ الظالمين»: The majority read it with kasra, as resumptive. Muslim ibn Jundub and al-Aʿraj read it with fatḥa, conjoined to «كلمةُ», the two conjoined items being separated by the answer of «لولا»; its implied form is: "were it not for a word and the settledness of the wrongdoers in the punishment, it would have been decided." It is parallel to {وَلَوْلاَ كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَّبِّكَ لَكَانَ لِزَاماً وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى} [Ṭā Hā: 129].

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَهُوَ وَاقِعٌ بِهِمْ}: i.e. and the apprehension, or and the punishment. As for «روضاتُ الجنَّات», the Shaykh said: "The common usage is sukūn on the wāw, and the dialect of Hudhayl is fatḥa on the wāw, treating it like a sound [root], as in «جَفَنات»; no one, as far as we know, read in their dialect." I say: if he meant that no one read in their dialect in this category as such, it is not so, because I presented to you in Sūrat al-Nūr that al-Aʿmash read {ثَلاَثُ عَوْرَاتٍ} [al-Nūr: 58] with fatḥa on the wāw. If he meant that it was not read in «رَوْضات» specifically — and that is not the apparent sense of his wording — that is possible.
His saying: «عندَ رَبِّهم»: It may be an adverb of «يَشاؤُون» — so said al-Ḥawfī — or of the [notion of] settledness that governs «لهم» — so said al-Zamakhsharī; the "being with" is figurative.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {يُبَشِّرُ الله عِبَادَهُ}: like His saying {كالذي خاضوا} [al-Tawba: 69], whose verification has preceded; the readings in «يُبَشِّر» have also preceded. Mujāhid and Ḥumayd ibn Qays read «يُبْشِرُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, sukūn on the bāʾ and kasra on the shīn, from «أَبْشَر», transferred from «بَشِر» with kasra, not from «بَشَر» with fatḥa, because the latter is transitive. The doubling in «بَشَّر» is for intensity, not for transitivity, since it is transitive without it. The Shaykh transmitted the reading «يَبْشُرُ», with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the shīn, from Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī among the Seven, and did not mention others of the Seven, whereas Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr agreed with them on that. «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the relative after it is its khabar (predicate), its returning pronoun being omitted by the stepwise process mentioned at His saying {كالذي خاضوا}, i.e. «يُبَشِّرُ به», then «يُبَشِّره» by extension. On the view of Yūnus, however, it needs no returning pronoun, because for him it is maṣdariyya — and that is also the view of al-Farrāʾ — i.e. "that is Allah's giving glad tidings to His servants." «ذلك» points to the honour Allah has prepared for them.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or [it means] that glad-tiding with which Allah gives glad tidings to His servants." The Shaykh said: "This is not apparent, since neither the word «البُشْرى» nor anything indicating it, such as «بَشَّر» or the like, has preceded in this sūra."
His saying: «إلاَّ المودَّةَ»: There are two views on it. First: it is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), since it is not of the genus of the wage. Second: it is connected, i.e. "I ask of you no wage for it except this," which is that you love the people of my kinship; and this was not a wage in reality, because his kinship was their kinship, so maintaining ties with them was binding on them by virtue of honour — so said al-Zamakhsharī. He also said: "If you say: why was it not said «إلاَّ مودةَ القُرْبَى» or «إلاَّ المودةَ للقُرْبى»? I say: they were made a place for love and a seat of it, as in your saying 'I have in the family of so-and-so a love.' «في» is not a complement of «المودة» like the lām when you say «إلاَّ المودةَ للقربى»; it is attached only to an omitted [word], as the adverbial phrase is attached in your saying 'the money is in the purse,' its implied form being 'except love established in the kinship and firmly seated in it.'" I say: the best I have heard on the meaning of this verse is the account of al-Shaʿbī, who said: "People pressed us much about this verse, so we wrote to Ibn ʿAbbās asking him about it. He wrote: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was of the most central lineage among Quraysh; there was no clan of theirs but had borne him [i.e. was related to him by birth]. So Allah the Exalted said: Say, I ask of you no wage for it except that you love me for my kinship with you; so observe what is between me and you, and believe me."
Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It has been said: connected, i.e. I ask of you nothing except love." I say: there is a question in his interpreting it as connected by what he mentioned, because he brought «شيء» which is general; and there is no disconnected exception that cannot be interpreted by what he mentioned. Do you not see that of your saying «ما جاءني أحدٌ إلاَّ حمارٌ» ("no one came to me except a donkey") it is sound to say «ما جاءني شيءٌ إلاَّ حماراً» ("nothing came to me except a donkey")?
Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «مَوَدَّة» without alif and lām.
His saying: {نَّزِدْ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْناً}: The majority read «نَزِدْ» with the nūn of majesty. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿAbd al-Wārith from Abū ʿAmr [read] «يَزِدْ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. Allah will increase. The majority read «حُسْناً» with tanwīn, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) on the pattern fuʿl, like «شُكْر»; it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ʿAbd al-Wārith from Abū ʿAmr [read] «حُسْنى» with the alif of the feminine, on the pattern of «بُشْرَى» and «رُجْعَى»; it is also a direct object. It may be an adjective, like «فُضْلَى», so it would describe an omitted noun, i.e. "a fine trait."

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {وَيَمْحُ الله الباطل}: This is resumptive, not included in the apodosis of the condition, because Allah the Exalted effaces falsehood absolutely. The wāw was dropped from it in pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters in continuous speech, and in writing, construing the script according to the pronunciation, as they wrote {سَنَدْعُ الزبانية} [al-ʿAlaq: 18] that way. But it ought to be that pausing on this is not permissible, because if one pauses on it with the original, namely the wāw, we contradict the script of the codex, and if we pause without it in agreement with the script, we contradict the original; a discussion of the like of this has passed for you. Makkī forbade pausing on the like of {وَمَن تَقِ السيئات} [Ghāfir: 9] and its category.
His saying: «ما تَفْعَلُون»: The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «تَفْعلون» with the upper-dotted tāʾ, looking to His saying «عن عبادِه», and the rest with the address, turning to people in general. [Translator's note: as written, the source attributes the tāʾ reading to Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Ḥafṣ and then says "the rest with the address," although the tāʾ is itself the address; the justification "looking to «عن عبادِه»" fits the yāʾ (third-person) reading. The two justifications appear to be swapped in the text; translated as written.]

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {وَيَسْتَجِيبُ الذين آمَنُواْ}: it is possible that the relative noun is the agent, i.e. they answer their Lord when He calls them, like His saying: {استجيبوا للَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُم} [al-Anfāl: 24]. Istajāba is like ajāba. From it is the verse:

3973 - A caller called, "Who will answer to generosity?" ... and no answerer answered him at that point

It is also possible that the sīn is for seeking, in its usual sense, meaning: the believers are summoned to answer on behalf of their Lord through righteous deeds. It is also possible that the relative noun is the direct object and the agent is a latent pronoun referring to Allah, meaning: Allah answers those who believe, i.e. when they call Him. It was also said: there is an implied lām, i.e. "Allah answers those who believe" [li-lladhīna āmanū], and He omitted it because it is known.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {مِن بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُواْ}: «مَا» is maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "after their despair". The majority read the nūn with fatḥa. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read it with kasra, which is a dialect, and on it «يَقْنِطُ» was read, as was {لاَ تَقْنَطُواْ} [al-Zumar: 53], whereas in the mutawātir reading the nūn has fatḥa. The kasra was not read in the past tense except as an irregular reading.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {وَمَا بَثَّ}: it may be genitive in position, conjoined to «السماواتِ», or nominative, conjoined to «خَلْقُ» with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "and the creation of what He dispersed". Al-Shaykh said this. There is a point to consider in it, because it comes back to making it genitive by annexation to the implied «خَلْق», so one does not turn away from that.

His saying: «فيهما», i.e. the heavens and the earth. But the heaven has no living beings in it, so it was said: it is like His saying: {نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 61] and {يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا الُّلؤْلُؤُ وَالمَرْجَانُ} [al-Raḥmān: 22]. It was also said: rather, He created in the heaven those that move. It was also said: among the angels are those who walk as well as fly. Al-Fārisī said: "It is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. 'and what He dispersed in one of the two'", and this is an enigma in speech.

His saying: «إذا يَشاء»: «إذا» is accusative by «جَمْعِهم», not by «قديرٌ». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because that would lead to the meaning being: 'He is able to gather them when He wills', so that power would be connected to will, which is impossible." I say: I do not know why it would be impossible according to the school of Ahl al-Sunna. If he follows the doctrine of the Muʿtazila, namely that power is connected to what Allah has not willed, his statement would stand, but that is a bad doctrine in which belief is not permitted. We say: it is also permissible for the adverbial to be connected to it.

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {فَبِمَا}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «بما» without the fāʾ. The others read «فبما» with it. In the first reading «مَا» is apparently a relative noun meaning "that which", and the khabar (predicate) is the preposition and its genitive noun in «بما كَسَبَتْ». A group, among them Abū l-Baqāʾ, said: it is conditional, with the fāʾ omitted from it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "like His saying {وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ} [al-Anʿām: 121], and the poet's saying:

3974 - Whoever does good deeds, Allah will thank him for them ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ."

This is not the doctrine of the majority; only al-Akhfash and some of the Baghdadis said it. As for the verse, «إنَّكم لَمُشْرِكون» is not the apodosis of the condition; it is the answer to an implied oath whose preparatory lām was omitted before the conditional particle.

As for the second reading, it is apparently conditional there, and no attention is paid to Abū l-Baqāʾ's statement that "it is weak". It is also possible that it is the relative noun, with the fāʾ entering the khabar by likening the relative noun to the condition, under conditions that I have set out fully in its place, praise be to Allah the Exalted. Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir agreed with their codices, for the fāʾ is absent from the codices of Medina and Syria, while the others agreed with theirs, for it is present in the codices of Mecca and Iraq.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {الجوار}: i.e. the ships that run. If you say: whenever an adjective is not specific to what it describes, omitting the described noun is impossible. You do not say "I passed by a walker", because walking is general. You do say "I passed by an engineer and a writer". And running is not among the specific attributes, so what is the explanation for this? The answer: / His saying «في البحر» is an indication pointing to the described noun. It is also possible that this is a predominant adjective, like «الأَبْطَح» and «الأَبْرَق», so it follows the governing agents without its described noun.

«في البحر» is attached to «الجوَاري» when it is not treated like the inert nouns. If it is treated like them, it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it. Likewise His saying «كالأَعْلام» is a ḥāl, i.e. resembling the banners, which are the mountains, like the saying of al-Khansāʾ:

3975 - Truly Ṣakhr is the one whom the guides take as their leader ... as if he were a banner with fire on its top

It was also heard: «هذه الجَوارُ», «وركبْتُ الجوارَ», «وفي الجوارِ», with the case ending on the rā', in forgetfulness of what was omitted. This has already been mentioned at His saying {وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 41] in al-Aʿrāf.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {فَيَظْلَلْنَ}: the majority read the lām that is the ʿayn (middle radical) with fatḥa, which is the regular form, because the past tense has kasra. You say ظَلِلْتُ قائماً. Qatāda read it with kasra, which is irregular, like حَسِب يَحْسِب and its sisters, which have already been mentioned. . . Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is from ظَلَّ يَظَلُّ and يَظِلُّ, like ضَلَّ يَضَلُّ and يَضِلُّ." Al-Shaykh said: "It is not as he said, because يَضَلُّ with fatḥa on the ʿayn is from ضَلِلْتُ with kasra in the past tense, and يَضِلُّ with kasra is from ضَلَلْتُ with fatḥa, and both are regular." He means that each of them has an origin it goes back to, unlike «ظَلَّ», whose past tense has kasra on the ʿayn only.

The nūn is its ism (subject) and «ورَواكدَ» its khabar. It is also possible that «ظَلَّ» here means "became", because the meaning does not concern the time of staying all day, which is only the daytime. It is the like of «أين باتَتْ يدُه» from this standpoint. Rukūd means being fixed and settled. He said:

3976 - And its stars stood still in the middle of the sky ... a standing still in the valley of the scattered herd of gazelles

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ}: conjoined to «يُسْكِنْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "because the meaning is: if He wills, He calms the wind and they stand still, or He lets it blow violently and they drown through its blowing."

Al-Shaykh said: "It is not necessarily the implied form 'or He lets it blow violently and they drown', because the destruction of the ships is not necessarily by the blowing of the wind; He may rather destroy them by tearing out a plank or by sinking." I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not state that this is necessary; he only mentioned something fitting, because His saying «يُسْكِنِ الريحَ» is matched by «يعْصِفْها», which is the height of excellence and antithesis.

His saying: «ويَعْفُ»: the majority read it jussive, conjoined to the apodosis of the condition. Al-Qushayrī found it problematic and said: "because the meaning is: if He wills, He calms the wind and those ships remain standing still, or destroys them through the sins of their people. So conjoining «ويَعْفُ» to this is not good, because the meaning would become 'if He wills, He pardons', and the meaning is not that. Rather, the meaning is a report of pardon without the condition of will. So it is conjoined to the jussive in respect of the wording, not in respect of the meaning. Some read «ويَعْفُو» with nominative, and it is good in meaning." Al-Shaykh said: "What he said is not good, since he did not understand the import of the construction and the meaning, except that if He wills, Allah destroys some people and saves others by way of pardoning them."

Al-Aʿmash read «ويَعْفُوْ» with the wāw. It may be like the jussive, with the wāw retained in the jussive just as the yāʾ is retained in {مَن يَتَّقِ وَيِصْبِرْ} [Yūsuf: 90]. It may also be that the verb is nominative, Allah the Exalted informing that He pardons many sins. Some of the people of Medina read it with accusative, with an implied «أَنْ» after the wāw, like its accusative in the saying of al-Nābigha:

3977 - If Abū Qābūs perishes, there perishes ... the spring pasture of the people and the sacred land
and after him we take hold of the tail of a life ... with a stunted back, having no hump

with «ونَأْخُذ» accusative, nominative and jussive. This is as it was read in the three ways after the fāʾ in His saying {فَيَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ} [al-Baqara: 284], whose exposition has already been given at the end of al-Baqara. The interpreted maṣdar from the implied «أَنْ» and the verb is conjoined to an imagined maṣdar derived from the verb before it, its implied form being: "or there occurs a destruction and a pardoning of many." So the accusative reading is like the jussive reading in meaning, except that in this one an interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to an imagined maṣdar, while in that one a verb is conjoined to its like.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {وَيَعْلَمَ الذين يُجَادِلُونَ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with nominative. The others read it with accusative. It was also read with jussive. As for the nominative, it is very clear, and it admits two analyses: a resumptive verbal sentence, or a resumptive nominal sentence, in which case you imply a mubtadaʾ before the verb, i.e. "and He knows those who". So «الذين» in the first is the fāʿil (agent) and in the second the mafʿūl (object). As for the accusative reading, it has several analyses. The first: al-Zajjāj said: "by ṣarf (diversion)." He said: "The meaning of ṣarf is diverting the conjunction from the wording to a conjunction on the meaning." He said: "That is because, when conjoining «ويعلَمْ» as a jussive to what precedes it was not good, since the meaning would be: 'if He wills, He knows', it was turned to conjoin it to the maṣdar of the preceding verb. That is only possible with an implied «أنْ», so that it is, together with the verb, in the interpretation of a noun."

The second: the saying of the Kufans that it is accusative by the wāw of ṣarf. They mean that the wāw itself is the accusative-assigner, not by an implied «أنْ». The meaning of ṣarf has already been given.

The third: al-Fārisī said, and al-Zamakhsharī reported it from al-Zajjāj, that the accusative is on an implied «أنْ», because before it is a condition. You say «ما تصنعْ أصنعْ وأكرمَك»; if you wish, «وأكرمُك», meaning "and I honour you"; and if you wish, «وأكرمْك» jussive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "There is a point to consider in it, because of what Sībawayh cited in his book." He said: "Know that the accusative with the wāw and the fāʾ in 'إنْ تَأْتِني آتِك وأعطيكَ' is weak, and it is something like the saying:

3978 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . and I join the Hijaz, and so I rest

This is not permitted, because it is not the norm of speech nor its way, except that in a condition it became a little stronger, because the doing is not obligatory unless an act has come from the first. Since it resembled what does not make it obligatory, such as the interrogative and the like, they permitted it with its weakness." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is not permitted to take the widely transmitted reading as being on a pattern that is not the norm of speech nor its way, and had it been of this type, Sībawayh would not have left it out of his book, for he mentioned its like among the problematic verses."

The fourth: that it is accusative by conjunction to an omitted causal clause, its implied form being: "so that He takes vengeance on them and knows those who". Conjunction to an omitted causal clause is not rare in the Qur'an. Among it: {وَلِنَجْعَلَهُ آيَةً لِّلْنَّاسِ} [Maryam: 21], and «وخَلَق اللَّهُ السماواتِ والأرضَ بالحقِّ، ولِتُجْزَى». Al-Zamakhsharī said this. Al-Shaykh said: "The implied 'so that He takes vengeance on them' is remote, because the destruction of some people and the rescue of others followed from the condition, so 'so that He takes vengeance on them' is not good. As for the two verses, the lām may be attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: 'and so that We make it a sign for the people We did that', 'and so that every soul is recompensed We did that'. He often implies this verb with this lām when there is no verb to attach it to." I say: rather, implying «لينتقمَ» is good, because it returns in meaning to the destruction of some people that follows from the condition.

As for the jussive, al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how can the meaning be sound with the jussive of «ويعلَمْ»? I say: it is as if it were said: if He wills, He combines three things: destroying some people, saving others, and warning yet others." When it is read as a jussive the mīm takes kasra because of the meeting of two sākin letters.

His saying: {مَا لَهُمْ مِّن مَّحِيصٍ} is in the position of accusative, because it fills the place of the two objects of «العِلْم».

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {فَمَآ أُوتِيتُمْ}: «ما» is conditional. It is in the position of accusative as the second object of «أُوتِيتم», and the first is the pronoun of the addressees, which stands in the place of the agent. He only put the second first because it has the head of the sentence.

His saying: «مِنْ شَيءٍ» is a clarification of the conditional «ما» because of the vagueness in it.

His saying: «فمتاعُ»: the fāʾ is the apodosis of the condition, and «متاعُ» is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is enjoyment". His saying: {وَمَا عِندَ الله}: «ما» is a relative noun and the mubtadaʾ, «خيرٌ» is its khabar, and «الذين» is attached to «أَبْقَى».

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {والذين يَجْتَنِبُونَ}: a conjunction (nasaq) on the first «الذين». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«الذين يَجْتَنبون» is in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) for «للذين آمنوا». It may be in the position of accusative with an implied «أعني», or in the position of nominative on the implied form «هم»." This is a slip of his in the recitation, as if he believed that the Qur'an reads {وعلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ، والذين يَجْتَنِبُونَ}, and so he built three analyses on it, a corrupt construction.

His saying: «كبائرَ»: the two brothers [Translator's note: i.e. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read here and in al-Najm «كبيرَ الإِثم» in the singular. The others read «كبائرَ» in the plural in both sūras. The singular here has the sense of the plural, and the script admits both readings.

His saying: {وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُواْ}: this «إذا» is accusative by «يَغْفِرُون», and «يَغْفِرُون» is the khabar of «هم», and the whole sentence is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause), which is «يَجْتَنِبون», the implied form being: "and those who avoid and they forgive", a nominal sentence conjoined to a verbal one. It is also possible that «هم» is emphasis (tawkīd) of the agent in «غَضِبوا», and on this «يَغْفِرون» is the apodosis of the condition. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«هم» is a mubtadaʾ and «يَغْفِرون» the khabar, and the sentence is the apodosis of «إذا»." This is not correct, because if it were the apodosis of «إذا» it would be joined with the fāʾ. You say «إذا جاء زيدٌ فعمروٌ منطلق» and it is not permitted to say «عمروٌ ينطلق». It was also said: «هم» is nominative by an implied verb which the following «يَغْفِرون» explains, and when the verb was omitted the pronoun became detached. Al-Shaykh did not find this remote. He said: "It should be permitted in the school of Sībawayh, because he permitted it with the jussive particle. You say «إنْ يَنْطَلِقْ، زيدٌ يَنْطَلِق», its implied form being «ينطلِقْ زيدٌ ينطلِقْ». So «ينطلقْ» occurs as the apodosis and yet it explains the verb; this is likewise. Moreover, that / is permitted in the protasis after it, as in {إِذَا السمآء انشقت} [al-Inshiqāq: 1], so it should be permitted in its apodosis too."

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {هُمْ يَنتَصِرُونَ}: exactly like His saying {وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُواْ هُمْ يَغْفِرُونَ}, and what preceded applies to it. Except that here there is the further possibility that «هم» is emphasis of the accusative pronoun in «أصابَهم», emphasised by a nominative pronoun. The only thing in it is the separation between the emphasised and the emphasiser by the agent. Apparently this is not prohibited.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {وَلَمَنِ انتصر}: this is the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement). Al-Ḥawfī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it a lām of oath. That is not good if we make «مَنْ» conditional, as will come, because the earlier one should then have been answered, and here only the condition is answered. «مَنْ» may be conditional, which is the apparent view, and the fāʾ in «فأولئك» is the apodosis of the condition; or it may be a relative noun, with the fāʾ entering because of what you know of the resemblance of the relative noun to the condition. «ظُلْمِه» is a maṣdar annexed to the object. Al-Zamakhsharī supported it with the reading of those who read «بعدما ظُلِمَ» in the passive.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {وَلَمَن صَبَرَ}: the discussion of the lām is clear, as already given. If you make it conditional, then «إنَّ» is the answer to the implied oath, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted because it is indicated. If it is a relative noun, then «إنَّ ذلك» is the khabar. Al-Ḥawfī and others allowed that «مَنْ» is conditional and that «ذلك» is its apodosis with the fāʾ omitted, as it is omitted in the famous verse:

3979 - Whoever does good deeds. . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

On the linking element there are two views. One: it is the demonstrative, when the mubtadaʾ is intended by it, and then there is an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: "that is among those of firm resolve in affairs". Two: it is an omitted pronoun, its implied form being: "of the firm resolve in affairs from him", or "of him". His saying «ولَمَنْ صَبَرَ» is conjoined to His saying «ولَمَنِ انتصَرَ». The sentence «إنما السبيلُ» is parenthetical.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {يُعْرَضُونَ}: a ḥāl, because the seeing is visual. «خاشعين» is a ḥāl. The pronoun in «عليها» refers to the Fire, since «العذاب» indicates it.

Ṭalḥa read «من الذِّل» with kasra on the dhāl. The difference between al-dhull and al-dhill has already been given. «من الذُّل» is attached to «خاشعين», i.e. "because of". It was also said: it is attached to «يَنْظُرون». His saying «مِنْ طَرْفٍ»: «مِنْ» may be for the beginning of the range, or partitive, or have the sense of «الباء», and each has been said. Ṭarf was said to mean the organ, and it was also said to mean the maṣdar. It is said: طُرِفَتْ عَيْنُه تُطْرَفُ طَرْفاً, i.e. they look with a furtive glance.

His saying: {وَقَالَ الذين آمنوا}: it may keep its literal sense, with «يومَ القيامة» governed by «خَسِروا». It may also have the sense of "says", in which case «يوم القيامةِ» is governed by it.

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {يَنصُرُونَهُم}: an adjective of «أَوْلِياء», so its position may be judged genitive in view of the wording of what it describes, or nominative in view of its position, for it is the ism of «كان».

His saying: «مِنْ سبيلٍ» is either the agent or a mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:47-47.t: His saying: {مِنَ الله}: it may be attached to «يأتي», i.e. "there comes from Allah a day that cannot be turned back"; or it may be attached to an omitted element indicated by «لا مَرَدَّ له», i.e. "nothing turns back that day from what Allah has decreed in it". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be attached to «لا مَرَدَّ». Al-Shaykh rejected this on the ground that it would then be a lengthened construct, so it should have been declinable and accusative with tanwīn.

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {فَإِنَّ الإنسان}: this is an instance of the overt noun placed where the pronoun belongs, i.e. "for he is ungrateful". Abū l-Baqāʾ implied an omitted pronoun and said: "«فإنَّ الإِنسانَ منهم»".

semin-durr:50-50.t: His saying: {ذُكْرَاناً وَإِنَاثاً}: a ḥāl, and it is a necessary ḥāl. What made its coming so permissible is that it comes after something where the matter could be otherwise, because the meaning of «يُزَوِّجُهم» is "He pairs them". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did He put the females before the males first, though the males are put before them, and then return and put the males first? And why did He make the males definite after making the females indefinite? I say: because He mentioned affliction at the end of the first verse, and man's ingratitude through forgetting the earlier mercy, then followed it with mention of His dominion and will and the apportioning of children. So He put the females first, because the course of the speech is that He does what He wills, not what man wills, so mentioning the females, who are among what man does not will, was more important, and the more important must come first; and so that what follows might be the kind that the Arabs counted as an affliction, He mentioned affliction and put the males last. When He put them last, He made up for their delay, though they deserve precedence, by making them definite, because making them definite carries elevation and renown, as if He said: 'and He grants to whom He wills the well-known horsemen, those mentioned, who are not hidden from you'. Then after that He gave each of the two kinds its due of precedence and delay, and made known that putting the females first was not because of their priority but for another requirement, so He said: ذُكْرَاناً وإناثاً, as He said {إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وأنثى} [al-Ḥujurāt: 13] and {فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزوجين الذكر والأنثى} [al-Qiyāma: 39]."

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: / {أَن يُكَلِّمَهُ الله}: «أَنْ» and what it governs is the ism of «كان», and not the «khabar» of «ما». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«أَنْ» and the verb are in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ and what precedes is the khabar, or an agent of the preposition because of its reliance on the negative particle." It is as if he [slipped in the recitation, imagining that the Qur'an is: وما لبشَرٍ أَنْ يُكَلِّمه], although an answer to him is possible with some strain. «إلاَّ وَحْياً» may be a maṣdar, i.e. "except the speech of revelation". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because revelation is not of the genus of speech." There is a point to consider in this, because apparently it is a "vacated" exception (mufarraghan), and the vacated one is not described thus. It may also be a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl.

His saying: «أو يُرْسِل»: Nāfiʿ read «يُرْسِلُ» with nominative on the lām, and likewise «فيوحِيْ» with its yāʾ quiescent. The others read both as accusative. As for the first reading, it has three analyses. The first: it is nominative on an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "or He sends". The second: it is conjoined to «وَحْياً» as a ḥāl, because «وَحْياً» is also in the interpretation of a ḥāl, as if He said: "except as one who reveals or one who sends". The third: it is conjoined to what «من وراءه» is attached to, whose implied form is: "or lets be heard from behind a veil", and «وَحْياً» is in the position of ḥāl, with that implied element conjoined to it, and «أَوْ يُرْسِلُ» conjoined to that. The implied form is: "except as one who reveals, or one who lets be heard from behind a veil, or one who sends".

As for the second reading, it has three analyses. The first: that it is conjoined to the implied element to which {مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ} is attached, whose implied form is: "or He speaks to him from behind a veil". This implied verb is conjoined to «وَحْياً», and the meaning is: "except by revelation, or by letting be heard from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger". It is not permitted to conjoin it to «يكلِّمَه», because of the corruption of the meaning. I say: since the implied form would become "it is not for a human that Allah should send a messenger", which is corrupt in wording and meaning. Makkī said: "because it would entail the negation of the messengers and the negation of those to whom they are sent."

The second: that it is accusative by an implied «أنْ», and it and what it governs are conjoined to «وَحْياً», and «وَحْياً» is a ḥāl, so here too it is a ḥāl: [the implied form being: "except as one who reveals or one who sends"]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«وَحْياً» and «أَنْ يُرْسِلَ» are two maṣdars occurring in the place of ḥāl, because «أَنْ يُرْسِلَ» has the sense of «إرسالاً». And {مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ} is an adverbial occurring in the place of ḥāl as well, like His saying {وعلى جُنُوبِهِمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 191]. The implied form is: 'It is not right that He speak to anyone except as one who reveals, or one who lets be heard from behind a veil, or one who sends.'" Al-Shaykh rejected this on the ground that a maṣdar occurring in the place of ḥāl is not regular; al-Mubarrad only made regular that which is a species of the verb, so "أتيتُه رَكْضاً" is permitted, and "أَتَيْتُه بكاءً", meaning "weeping", is prohibited.

And on the ground that «أَنْ يُرْسِلَ» does not occur as a ḥāl, because Sībawayh stated explicitly that «أَنْ» and the verb do not occur as a ḥāl, whereas the explicit maṣdar does occur as a ḥāl: you say «جاء زيد ضَحِكاً», and «جاء أَنْ يضحكَ» is not permitted.

The third: that it is conjoined to the meaning of «وَحْياً», for it is a maṣdar interpreted as «أنْ» and the verb. The implied form is: "except by that it be revealed to him, or by that He send". Makkī and Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned it.

His saying: {أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابٍ}: the majority read the singular. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «حُجُبٍ» in the plural. This prepositional phrase is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being: "or He speaks to him from behind a veil". It has already been mentioned that this verb is conjoined to the meaning of «وَحْياً», i.e. "except that He reveal or speak to him". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is not permitted for «مِنْ» to be attached to the «يُكَلِّمَه» present in the wording, because what precedes the exception does not govern what follows it except" [Translator's note: the sentence breaks off thus in the source], then he said: "It was also said: «مِنْ» is attached to «يُكلِّمه» because it is an adverbial, and latitude is allowed in adverbials."

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {مَا كُنتَ تَدْرِي مَا الكتاب}: the first «ما» is negative and the second interrogative. The interrogative sentence suspends the act of knowing, so it is in the position of accusative, filling the place of two objects. The whole negated sentence is in the position of accusative as ḥāl from the kāf in «إليك». His saying «جَعَلْنَاه»: the pronoun refers either to «رُوْحاً», or to «الكتاب», or to both, because they serve one purpose, so it is like His saying {والله وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَن يُرْضُوهُ} [al-Tawba: 62].

Ibn Ḥawshab read «لتُهْدَى» in the passive. Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «لتُهْدي» with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the dāl, from ahdā.

His saying: «نَهْدِي» may be resumptive, or a repeated object of «الجَعْل», or an adjective of «نُوْراً».

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying: {صِرَاطِ الله}: a badal from the preceding «صراطٍ», a badal of the whole for the whole, of a definite noun for an indefinite. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبِّي عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ (١٠)).
His saying (ذَلِكُمُ): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «اللَّهُ» an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute), and «رَبِّي» the khabar (predicate). Or اللَّهُ may be the khabar, with رَبِّي a second khabar or a badal; or [رَبِّي] may be an adjective of [the name] Allah the Exalted, and «عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ» the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاطِرُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَمِنَ الْأَنْعَامِ أَزْوَاجًا يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ (١١)).
His saying (فَاطِرُ السَّمَاوَاتِ): i.e. "He is the Originator"; it may also be a further khabar (predicate).
It is also read in the genitive (فَاطِرِ), as a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ in «عَلَيْهِ». The hāʾ in «فِيهِ» is the pronoun of the making (al-jaʿl), which the verb has indicated; it may also be the pronoun of the created thing indicated by يَذْرَؤُكُمْ.
The kāf in «كَمِثْلِهِ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "nothing is like Him" (لَيْسَ مِثْلَهُ شَيْءٌ); so مِثْلَهُ is the khabar of لَيْسَ. If it were not redundant, it would lead to an impossibility, since the meaning would then be that He has a like, and that His like has no like; and in that there is a contradiction, because if He has a like, then His like has a like, namely Him — besides the fact that affirming a like for Allah, glory be to Him, is impossible.
It is also said: «مِثْلِ» is redundant, and the implied wording is "nothing is as He is" (لَيْسَ كَهُوَ شَيْءٌ), as in His saying (فَإِنْ آمَنُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ); this has been mentioned. This is a far-fetched view.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (شَرَعَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الدِّينِ مَا وَصَّى بِهِ نُوحًا وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى وَعِيسَى أَنْ أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ كَبُرَ عَلَى الْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يُنِيبُ (١٣)).
His saying (أَنْ أَقِيمُوا): it may be a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ in «بِهِ», or of «مَا», or of «مِنَ الدِّينِ» — each is suitable.
It may also be that «أَنْ» has the sense of أَيْ ("that is"), so that it has no grammatical position.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ وَالْمِيزَانَ وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ (١٧)).
His saying (لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ): it may have been put in the masculine according to the meaning of "the time", or according to the meaning of "the resurrection", or as a relational form (al-nasab), i.e. "possessed of nearness".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا وَهُوَ وَاقِعٌ بِهِمْ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فِي رَوْضَاتِ الْجَنَّاتِ لَهُمْ مَا يَشَاءُونَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ (٢٢)).
(وَهُوَ وَاقِعٌ): i.e. the requital of what they earned.
It is also said: it is the pronoun of the fearing (al-ishfāq).

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ قُلْ لَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّةَ فِي الْقُرْبَى وَمَنْ يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَزِدْ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْنًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ (٢٣)).
His saying (يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ): the pronoun referring back to الَّذِي is omitted, i.e. "gives glad tidings of it".
(إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّةَ): a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), or the reverse [Translator's note: so in the text]. It is also said: it is a connected exception, i.e. "I do not ask you for anything except love for kinship, for that I do ask of you".

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَإِنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلَى قَلْبِكَ وَيَمْحُ اللَّهُ الْبَاطِلَ وَيُحِقُّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (٢٤)).
His saying (يَخْتِمْ): it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (وَيَمْحُ): nominative, resumptive, and not part of the apodosis, because He erases falsehood without condition. The wāw was dropped from the pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and from the Muṣḥaf by following the pronunciation.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتُ وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَالْكَافِرُونَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ (٢٦)).
His saying (وَيَسْتَجِيبُ): it means "He answers".
And (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
It is also said: "He answers the prayer of those who believe".
It is also said: «الَّذِينَ» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. they submit to Him.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَثَّ فِيهِمَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ وَهُوَ عَلَى جَمْعِهِمْ إِذَا يَشَاءُ قَدِيرٌ (٢٩)).
His saying (إِذَا يَشَاءُ): what governs «إِذَا» is «جَمْعِهِمْ», not «قَدِيرٌ», because that would lead to the meaning becoming "and He is able to gather them when He wills", so that the power would be made dependent on the will; and that is impossible.
«عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to قَدِيرٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:3-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَلِكَ يُوحِي إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٣) لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ (٤)).
His saying (كَذَلِكَ يُوحِي): it is read with a yāʾ with ḍamma, in the active voice (ʿalā mā summiya fāʿiluhu, "with its agent named"); the fāʿil (agent) is (اللَّهُ) and what follows it is a naʿt (adjective) of it, and the kāf is in the position of the accusative by يُوحِي. It is also read in the passive (يُوحَى), and there are two views on that. The first: that «كَذَلِكَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يُوحَى» the khabar (predicate), and «اللَّهُ» is the agent of an omitted verb, as though it were asked "Who reveals?" and He said: "Allah"; and what follows it is a naʿt of it.
It is also possible that «الْعَزِيزُ» is a mubtadaʾ, with «الْحَكِيمُ» a naʿt of it or a khabar, and «لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ» a khabar, or a second khabar. The second view: that «كَذَلِكَ» is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and «إِلَيْكَ» is what stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); i.e. "a revelation like that".

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ (٣٠)).
His saying (وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ): «مَا» is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
(فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ) is its apodosis (jawāb), and what is meant by the two verbs is the future. Whoever among the Readers dropped the fāʾ (بِمَا كَسَبَتْ) construed it on the pattern of His saying (وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ), and of what occurs in the poet's saying:
مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الْحَسَنَاتِ اللَّهُ يَشْكُرُهَا
("Whoever does good deeds, Allah will thank them")
On this view, «مَا» may also be taken in the sense of الَّذِي (that which), but there is weakness in that.

ukberi-tibyan:32-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ الْجَوَارِ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ (٣٢) إِنْ يَشَأْ يُسْكِنِ الرِّيحَ فَيَظْلَلْنَ رَوَاكِدَ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ (٣٣) أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ بِمَا كَسَبُوا وَيَعْفُ عَنْ كَثِيرٍ (٣٤) وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِنَا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (٣٥)).
His saying (الْجِوَارِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), or a fāʿil (agent) made nominative by the preposition phrase; and «فِي الْبَحْرِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it, governed by [the notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār). «فِي» may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to الْجَوَارِي.
And (كَالْأَعْلَامِ) is, on the first view, a second ḥāl, and on the second it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «الْجَوَارِ». And (يُسْكِنِ) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (فَيَظْلَلْنَ) is conjoined to the apodosis, and likewise «أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ» and «يَعْفُ».
As for His saying (وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ): it is read in the accusative on the implied wording "and that He may know" (وَأَنْ يَعْلَمَ), because He turned it away from the apodosis and conjoined it according to the meaning.
It is also read with kasra (وَيَعْلَمِ), on the view that it is jussive (majzūm), vowelled because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It is also read in the nominative (وَيَعْلَمُ), as resumptive. His saying (مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ): the negated clause stands in place of the two objects of عَلِمْتُ.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ (٣٦)).
His saying (فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ): i.e. "then it is enjoyment".

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُوا هُمْ يَغْفِرُونَ (٣٧)).
His saying (وَالَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ): conjoined to His saying (لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ).
It may also be in the position of the accusative by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"), or of the nominative on the implied wording «هُمْ» ("they are").
And (كَبَائِرَ) is in the plural, its singular being كَبِيرَةٌ; whoever read it in the singular (كَبِيرَ) took it as the genus.
And (هُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «يَغْفِرُونَ» is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the answer to إِذَا.
It is also said: «هُمْ» is nominative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "they forgave" (غَفَرُوا); the verb was omitted because يَغْفِرُونَ indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَنْ صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ (٤٣)).
His saying (وَلَمَنْ صَبَرَ): «مَنْ» is conditional, and «صَبَرَ» is in the position of the jussive by it; the apodosis is (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ), the fāʾ having been omitted.
It is also said: «مَنْ» has the sense of الَّذِي (the one who), and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. "that, on his part, is…" (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ).

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لَهُمْ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ (٤٦)).
His saying (يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ): it may be in the position of the genitive, following the wording of the noun it qualifies, or in the nominative following its position.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُوا فَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا إِنْ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ وَإِنَّا إِذَا أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً فَرِحَ بِهَا وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَإِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ كَفُورٌ (٤٨)).
His saying (فَإِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ كَفُورٌ): i.e. "man among them" (إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْهُمْ) [Translator's note: i.e. the overt noun stands in place of the pronoun referring to them, with the referring element implied].

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَانًا وَإِنَاثًا وَيَجْعَلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ عَقِيمًا إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ (٥٠)).
His saying (ذُكْرَانًا وَإِنَاثًا): they are a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the meaning is: He pairs the two kinds together.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْيًا أَوْ مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ مَا يَشَاءُ إِنَّهُ عَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ (٥١)).
His saying (أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ): «أَنْ» with the verb is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate); or it is a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition phrase, since that leans on the particle of negation. And (إِلَّا وَحْيًا) is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because revelation (waḥy) is not speaking (taklīm).
(أَوْ مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ): the preposition is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "or that He speak to him"; and this omitted element is conjoined to «وَحْيًا», the implied wording being "except that it be revealed to him, or that He speak to him". «مِنْ» cannot be attached to the يُكَلِّمَهُ present in the wording, because what precedes a disconnected exception does not govern what comes after «إِلَّا».
As for (أَوْ يُرْسِلَ): whoever read it in the accusative [takes it as] conjoined to the position of «وَحْيًا», i.e. He sends an angel to him.
It is also said: it is in the position of the genitive, i.e. "by His sending" (بِأَنْ يُرْسِلَ). It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It cannot be conjoined to «أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ», because its meaning would then become "it is not for a human being that Allah should speak to him, nor that He should send a messenger to him", and this is unsound; and also because conjoining it to the أَنْ يُكَلِّمَ that is present would bring it into the ṣila (relative clause) of أَنْ, and «إِلَّا وَحْيًا» would separate one part of the ṣila from another, since it is disconnected.
Whoever read يُرْسِلُ in the nominative made it resumptive.
It is also said: «مِنْ» is attached to يُكَلِّمَهُ, because it is an adverbial phrase, and latitude is allowed with adverbial phrases.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا مَا كُنْتَ تَدْرِي مَا الْكِتَابُ وَلَا الْإِيمَانُ وَلَكِنْ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُورًا نَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ نَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٥٢)).
His saying (مَا كُنْتَ تَدْرِي): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the kāf in «إِلَيْكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (صِرَاطِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَلَا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَصِيرُ الْأُمُورُ (٥٣)).
His saying (صِرَاطِ اللَّهِ): it is a badal (substitute) of (صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) — a definite substituted for an indefinite. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ الْقُرَى وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَتُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ الْجَمْعِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَرِيقٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيقٌ فِي السَّعِيرِ (٧)).
His saying (فَرِيقٌ): it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "some of them are a party in the Garden and some of them are a party in the Blaze". The implied wording may also be "among them is a party".

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَهُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَلَكِنْ يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ وَالظَّالِمُونَ مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ (٨)).
His saying (وَالظَّالِمُونَ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate). The accusative was not good, because in the clause after it there is no verb that would explain the governor of the accusative.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat "al-Shūrā" ("Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf"), Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حم﴾ ﴿عسق﴾ [al-Shūrā: 2] — we have already explained the letters of the alphabet. It has come in the commentary that these letters are one of the names of Allah. It was also transmitted as "حـم سـق" without ʿayn, but in the codices the ʿayn is clearly present.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿جَعَلَ لَكم مِن أنْفُسِكم أزْواجًا ومِنَ الأنْعامِ أزْواجًا﴾, that is: He created the male and the female of all animals.
And His saying: ﴿يَذْرَؤُكم فِيهِ﴾, that is: He multiplies you by making pairs of you and of the livestock.
And His saying: ﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ﴾ — this kāf is emphatic, and the meaning is: "there is nothing like Him". It is not permissible to say that the meaning is "there is nothing like the like of Him", because whoever says this has affirmed a like for Allah — exalted is He far above that.

zajjaj:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿شَرَعَ لَكم مِنَ الدِّينِ ما وصّى بِهِ نُوحًا﴾ — it is related in the commentary that the first to bring the prohibition of [marrying] daughters, sisters and mothers was Nūḥ. ﴿والَّذِي أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ وما وصَّيْنا بِهِ إبْراهِيمَ ومُوسى وعِيسى﴾, that is: "and He has ordained for you what He enjoined upon Ibrāhīm, Mūsā and ʿĪsā".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أنْ أقِيمُوا الدِّينَ ولا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ﴾ is an explanation of His saying: ﴿وَما وصَّيْنا بِهِ إبْراهِيمَ﴾. The position of "أنْ" may be accusative, nominative or genitive. The accusative is in the sense: "He ordained for you that you establish the religion"; the nominative is in the sense: "it is: that you establish the religion"; and the genitive is as a badal (substitute) from the bāʾ [i.e. from the pronoun governed by بِهِ], and the genitive is the most far-fetched of these aspects. It is also permissible that "أنْ أقِيمُوا الدِّينَ" be an explanation of what He enjoined upon Nūḥ, and of His saying ﴿والَّذِي أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ﴾, and of His saying ﴿وَما وصَّيْنا بِهِ إبْراهِيمَ﴾, so that the meaning would be: "He ordained for you and for those before you the establishing of the religion and the abandoning of division, and He ordained unity in following the messengers".

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَبِّكَ إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, that is: "and the People of the Book did not divide except with knowledge that division is misguidance, but they did that out of envy (بَغْيًا)", that is: for the sake of transgression. [Translator's note: the explanation here concerns the earlier part of the verse, ﴿وَما تَفَرَّقُوا إلّا مِن بَعْدِ ما جاءَهُمُ العِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, though the lemma quoted is the later clause.]
And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَبِّكَ إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى لَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, that is: they would have been requited for their deeds. The word is His deferring of the Hour; what indicates that is His saying: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿فَلِذَلِكَ فادْعُ واسْتَقِمْ كَما أُمِرْتَ﴾ — its meaning is: to that, then, call, and be steadfast; that is: to the establishing of the religion call, and be steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires. ﴿وَقُلْ آمَنتُ بِما أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ مِن كِتابٍ﴾, that is: I believe in all of Allah's books, because those who divided believed in some of the books and disbelieved in some.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي أنْـزَلَ الكِتابَ بِالحَقِّ والمِيزانَ﴾ — "المِيزان" (the balance) is justice. ﴿وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ﴾ — "قَرِيبٌ" (masculine) is permissible only because the femininity of "السّاعَة" is not a real femininity, and it is in the sense of "perhaps the resurrection is near". It may also be in the sense: "perhaps the coming of the Hour is near".

zajjaj:18-18.t:
﴿يَسْتَعْجِلُ بِها الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِها﴾, that is: whoever thinks he will not be resurrected seeks to hasten it.
And His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مُشْفِقُونَ مِنها﴾ — because they know that they will be resurrected and held to account. ﴿ألا إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُمارُونَ في السّاعَةِ لَفي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾, that is: those into whom doubt and uncertainty about the Hour enter, so that they dispute about it and deny its occurrence, ﴿لَفِي ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾, because if they reflected, they would know that the One who originated them and created them from dust, then from a drop of semen, then from a clot, until they reached their full growth, is able to originate them [again] and resurrect them.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَن كانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الآخِرَةِ نَـزِدْ لَهُ في حَرْثِهِ ومَن كانَ يُرِيدُ حَرْثَ الدُّنْيا نُؤْتِهِ مِنها وما لَهُ في الآخِرَةِ مِن نَصِيبٍ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that its meaning is: "whoever desires the work of the Hereafter...". So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is that whoever desires the reward of the work of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tillage, that is: We grant him success and multiply good deeds for him; and whoever desires the tillage of this world — that is, whoever aims only at a share of this world — while not believing in the Hereafter, We give him of this world, that is: We provide for him from this world, not that he is given everything he wants. And if he does not believe in the Hereafter, he has no share in the good which reaches [people] from the work of the Hereafter.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿تَرى الظّالِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمّا كَسَبُوا وهو واقِعٌ بِهِمْ﴾, that is: you see them fearful of the recompense of what they earned, and the recompense of what they earned is the Fire. ﴿وَهُوَ واقِعٌ بِهِمْ﴾, that is: and the recompense of their earning will befall them.
﴿والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ في رَوْضاتِ الجَنّاتِ لَهم ما يَشاءُونَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾, that is: "the wrongdoers will have the Fire, and the believers will have the Garden".

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ عِبادَهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ — it is read "يُبَشِّرُ", "يَبْشُرُ" and "يُبْشِرُ".
And His saying: ﴿قُلْ لا أسْألُكم عَلَيْهِ أجْرًا إلا المَوَدَّةَ في القُرْبى﴾, that is: except that you love me for my kinship [with you]. It has come in the commentary from Ibn ʿAbbās — may Allah have mercy on him — that he said: "There is no clan of Quraysh but the Prophet ﷺ has kinship in it." And it is related «that the Prophet ﷺ said to Quraysh: "You are my kin, and the first to answer me and obey me"». And it is related «that the Anṣār came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Allah has guided us through you, and you are our sister's son"», and they brought him money to help him with what befell him, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿قُلْ لا أسْألُكم عَلَيْهِ أجْرًا إلا المَوَدَّةَ في القُرْبى﴾. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the accusative of "المَوَدَّةَ" is by its being in the sense of an exception not of the same kind as the first (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), not in the sense "I ask of you, as a reward for it, love for kinship", because the prophets — the blessings of Allah be upon them — do not ask a reward for conveying the message. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "but I remind you of love for kinship". His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَـزِدْ لَهُ فِيها حُسْنًا﴾, that is: whoever does a good deed, We multiply it for him. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ﴾: forgiving of sins, accepting of repentance, rewarding it.

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرى عَلى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَإنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلى قَلْبِكَ ويَمْحُ اللَّهُ الباطِلَ﴾ — its meaning is: "if Allah wills, He will make you forget what has come to you"; so said Qatāda. It is also possible that "فَإنْ يَشَإ اللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلى قَلْبِكَ" means: He will fortify your heart with patience in the face of their harm and their saying "he has fabricated a lie against Allah". "وَيَمْحُ اللَّهُ الباطِلَ": the pause on it is "وَيَمْحُوا", with wāw and alif, because the meaning is: "and Allah erases falsehood in any case" [i.e. it is not part of the jussive apodosis]. It was written in the codex without wāw because the wāw drops in pronunciation due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it was written according to the connected pronunciation, while the wāw is established in the wording. The proof of it is: ﴿وَيُحِقُّ الحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ﴾, that is: "and Allah erases polytheism, and establishes the truth by what He has revealed of His Book on the tongue of His Prophet, peace be upon him".

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ — the meaning is: "and He answers those who believe and do righteous deeds".

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُنَـزِّلُ الغَيْثَ مِن بَعْدِ ما قَنَطُوا ويَنْشُرُ رَحْمَتَهُ﴾ — and it is read "قَنِطُوا" with kasra on the nūn. One says "قَنَطَ، يَقْنِطُ" and "قَنِطَ، يَقْنَطُ" when one despairs. It is related that it was said to ʿUmar: "The land has become barren and the people have despaired", and he said: "Then they will be rained upon", because of this verse.

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ يُوحِي إلَيْكَ وإلى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾ — it was read "يُوحى" (passive), and it was read "نُوحِي إلَيْكَ وإلى الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكَ" with the nūn. It has come in the commentary that "Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf" was revealed to every prophet before Muḥammad — may Allah bless him and all of them. The position of the kāf of "كَذَلِكَ" is accusative; the meaning is: "Like that He reveals to you...".
