Whoever reads "يُوحِي" with the yāʾ, the name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is made nominative by its verb, which is "يُوحِي". Whoever reads "يُوحى إلَيْكَ", the name of Allah explains [who did the action] for a verb whose agent is not named. Like this in poetry:
لِيُبْكَ يَزِيدٌ ضارِعٌ لِخُصُومَةٍ ∗∗∗ ومُخْتَبِطٌ مِمّا تُطِيحُ الطَّوائِحُ
(Let Yazīd be wept for — [let him be wept for by] one humbled in a dispute, and one seeking favour when calamities sweep [his wealth] away.)
So he made clear who ought to weep for him. Whoever reads "نُوحِي إلَيْكَ" with the nūn makes "نُوحِي" a statement about Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, makes "اللَّهُ" nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and makes "العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ" the khabar (predicate) of "اللَّهُ"; or, if he wishes, "العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ" is an attribute of "اللَّهُ", Mighty and Majestic is He, nominative just as the name of Allah is nominative, and the khabar is ﴿لَهُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 4]

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما أصابَكم مِن مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِما كَسَبَتْ أيْدِيكم ويَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ في آياتِنا﴾ [al-Shūrā: 35]. In the codex of the people of Medina it is "بِما كَسَبَتْ أيْدِيكم" without fāʾ, and so they read it, except Abū Jaʿfar, who retains the fāʾ. In the codices of the people of Iraq it is with the fāʾ, and so is their reading, and it is better in Arabic, because the fāʾ is the requital-particle of the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the meaning is: "whatever calamity befalls you, it is because of what your hands have earned". And "ويَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ يُجادِلُونَ" (nominative) was read; the accusative is by implying "أنْ", because before it there is a conditional requital. You say: "ما تَصْنَعْ أصْنَعْ مِثْلَهُ وأُكْرِمَكَ" (whatever you do I will do the like, and honour you — accusative); and if you wish you say "وأُكْرِمُكَ" (nominative), meaning "and I honour you"; and if you wish "وأُكْرِمْكَ", in the jussive.
It is related from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «"Allah is too generous to repeat the punishment upon His servant"», that is: when a calamity befalls him in this world because of what his hands have earned, He does not repeat the punishment upon him in the Hereafter. As for whoever reads "وما أصابَكم مِن مُصِيبَةٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ أيْدِيكم ويَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ", [the meaning is]: He does not requite much of what your hands have earned in this world. It is also possible that He pardons much, so that He does not requite it either in this world or in the Hereafter. And the meaning of ﴿ما لَهم مِن مَحِيصٍ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 35] is: "they have no way of turning aside and no escape". One says "حاصَ عَنْهُ" when one moves away from it, and one says "حاضَ عَنْهُ" in the sense of "حاصَ"; but it is not permissible to read "ما لَهم مِن مَحِيضٍ", even though the meaning is the same. As for the position of "الَّذِينَ" in His saying: ﴿وَيَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَمِلُوا الصّالِحاتِ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 26], it may be accusative and it may be nominative. Whoever takes it as accusative does so in the sense: "and Allah answers those who believe and do righteous deeds"; and whoever takes it as nominative does so in the sense: "those who believe and do righteous deeds respond to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He", that is: to what Allah calls them to.

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبائِرَ الإثْمِ والفَواحِشَ﴾ — the position of "الَّذِينَ" is genitive, an attribute of His saying: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وعَلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 36]. As for "كَبائِرَ الإثْمِ" (the major sins), some of them said: everything for which Allah has promised the Fire is a major sin. It was said: the major sins are [those] from the beginning of Sūrat "al-Nisāʾ", from His saying: ﴿وَلا تَتَبَدَّلُوا الخَبِيثَ بِالطَّيِّبِ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 2], up to His saying: ﴿إنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 31]. And it has been said: the major sins are: associating partners with Allah, killing a soul which Allah has made sacred, slandering chaste women, disobedience to parents, consuming the property of the orphan, fleeing from the advancing army, and treating the forbidden as lawful.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والَّذِينَ اسْتَجابُوا لِرَبِّهِمْ وأقامُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾ — "الَّذِينَ" is also in the position of the genitive, in the sense: "and what is with Allah is better and more lasting for those who believe and for those who respond to their Lord and establish the prayer".
And His saying: ﴿وَأمْرُهم شُورى بَيْنَهُمْ﴾, that is: they do not act on an opinion individually until they agree upon it. And it was said: no people ever consulted one another without being guided to the best of what was available to them.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
﴿والَّذِينَ إذا أصابَهُمُ البَغْيُ هم يَنْتَصِرُونَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary that they disliked abasing themselves, lest the wicked become bold against them. And it is related that it was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.
If someone says: are they praised for avenging themselves or not? It is said: they are praised, because whoever avenges himself and takes his right without exceeding in that what Allah has commanded — not going to excess in killing, if he is the next of kin of a slain person, nor in retaliation — is obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and every obedient one is praised. Likewise whoever avoids sins is praised, and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿إنْ تَجْتَنِبُوا كَبائِرَ ما تُنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ نُكَفِّرْ عَنْكم سَيِّئاتِكم ونُدْخِلْكم مُدْخَلا كَرِيمًا﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 31]

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَزاءُ سَيِّئَةٍ سَيِّئَةٌ مِثْلُها﴾ — the first is an evil deed in wording and in meaning, and the second is an evil deed in wording only; the one who does it is not an evildoer, but it was called an evil deed because it is the requital of an evil, for evil is requited only with its like, and requiting with it is not an evil deed that entails sin. It was called "سَيِّئَةٌ" only so that it would be known that the one who wounds and the offender is retaliated against in the measure of his offence. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَمَنِ اعْتَدى عَلَيْكم فاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ ما اعْتَدى عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Baqara: 194]; its interpretation is: repay him with its like. The speech of the Arabs runs on this pattern.

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying: ﴿وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وغَفَرَ إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِن عَزْمِ الأُمُورِ﴾, that is: the patient one is given a reward for his patience, so everyone whose desire for the reward increases is of the most complete resolve. Some of the lexicographers have said that the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿واتَّبِعُوا أحْسَنَ ما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكم مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [al-Zumar: 55] is that it includes retaliation and pardon, and pardon is the best of it.

zajjaj:45-45.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ﴾ means: "they look at the Fire with a furtive glance". Some of them said: they will be gathered blind, and will see the Fire with their hearts when they are exposed to it. And it was said: they look at it stealthily.

zajjaj:47-47.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما لَكم مِن مَلْجَإٍ يَوْمَئِذٍ وما لَكم مِن نَكِيرٍ﴾, that is: you have no one to rescue you from the punishment, and you will be unable to deny what you are confronted with of your sins, or the punishment that befalls you.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
His saying: ﴿يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشاءُ إناثًا ويَهَبُ لِمَن يَشاءُ الذُّكُورَ﴾ ﴿أوْ يُزَوِّجُهم ذُكْرانًا وإناثًا﴾ [al-Shūrā: 50], that is: and He makes the children He grants males and females. So the meaning of "يُزَوِّجُهم ذُكْرانًا وإناثًا" is: He pairs them. Any two of which one is coupled with the other are a pair (زَوْجان), each one of them being called "زَوْج". You say: "عِنْدِي زَوْجانِ مِنَ الخِفافِ" (I have a pair of khuffs), meaning that you have, in number, two, that is: "two khuffs". Likewise a woman and her husband are a pair.
And His saying: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُ مَن يَشاءُ عَقِيمًا﴾ [al-Shūrā: 50], that is: He makes the woman barren, she who does not give birth; and likewise "رَجُلٌ عَقِيمٌ" (a barren man) too, to whom no child is born; and likewise "الرِّيحُ العَقِيمُ" (the barren wind) is that from which neither rain nor any good comes.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿تَكادُ السَّماواتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِن فَوْقِهِنَّ﴾ — it was read "مِمَّنْ فَوْقَهُنَّ" (from the One above them), and it was read "يَنْفَطِرْنَ". The meaning of "يَنْفَطِرْنَ" and "يَتَفَطَّرْنَ" is: they split and are rent asunder. So the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: the heavens almost split from above them because of the greatness of Allah, because when He said ﴿وَهُوَ العَلِيُّ العَظِيمُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 4], He said: the heavens almost split because of His greatness. And likewise "يَنْفَطِرْنَ مِمَّنْ فَوْقَهُنَّ", that is: from the greatness of the One above them.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿والمَلائِكَةُ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ ويَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِمَن في الأرْضِ﴾ — the meaning of "يُسَبِّحُونَ" is: they magnify Allah and declare Him free of all evil; "and they seek forgiveness for those on earth among the believers". It is not possible that they seek forgiveness for everyone on earth, because Allah the Exalted said about the disbelievers: ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ والمَلائِكَةِ والنّاسِ أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [al-Baqara: 161]. In this is proof that the angels seek forgiveness only for the believers, and His saying in Sūrat "al-Muʾmin" indicates that: ﴿وَيَسْتَغْفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا رَبَّنا وسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وعِلْمًا﴾ [Ghāfir: 7]

zajjaj:51-51.t:
His saying: ﴿وَما كانَ لِبَشَرٍ أنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ إلا وحْيًا أوْ مِن وراءِ حِجابٍ أوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولا فَيُوحِيَ بِإذْنِهِ ما يَشاءُ﴾ — it is read "أوْ يُرْسِلُ" with the nominative of "يُرْسِلُ", and "فَيُوحِي" with the yāʾ quiescent. The commentary is that Allah's speech to humans is either by sending an angel to them, as He sent to His prophets, or from behind a veil, as He spoke to Mūsā, peace be upon him, or by an inspiration with which He inspires them. Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿أوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولا﴾ with the accusative, and he said: "يُرْسِلَ" is construed on "أنْ يُوحِيَ" — this one in His saying "أنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ". He said: because that is not the proper construal of the speech, since it would turn the meaning into: "it is not for a human that Allah should send a messenger", and that is not permissible; rather "يُرْسِلَ" is construed on "يُوحِيَ", the meaning being: "it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revealing, or by sending". [Translator's note: the sentence as printed is garbled; the sense of al-Khalīl's view (as in Sībawayh's Kitāb) is that «يُرْسِلَ» cannot be construed on «أنْ» in «أنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ», but on an implied «أنْ يُوحِيَ» underlying «وَحْيًا».] The nominative is permissible in "يُرْسِلُ" in the sense of a ḥāl (circumstantial), the meaning being: "it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except revealing, or sending a messenger — thus is His speech to them". The poet said:
وَخَيْلٍ قَدْ دَلَفْتُ لَها بِخَيْلٍ ∗∗∗ تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهِمْ ضَرْبٌ وجِيعُ
(Many a troop of horse I have advanced against with horse; the greeting between them is a painful striking.)
And like His saying "أوْ يُرْسِلَ" with the accusative is the poet's saying:
وَلَوْلا رِجالٌ مِن رِزامٍ أعِزَّةٌ ∗∗∗ وآلُ سُبَيْعٍ أوْ أسُوءَكَ عَلْقَما
(Were it not for mighty men of Rizām and the family of Subayʿ, or [were it not for] my grieving you, ʿAlqama...)
The meaning is: "or that I grieve you". And he said: it is permissible to put "أوْ يُرْسِلُ" in the nominative in the sense: "or He sends". This is the view of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and all whose knowledge is relied upon.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِن أمْرِنا﴾, that is: We did in revelation to you as We did with the messengers before you. The position of "كَذَلِكَ" is accusative, by His saying "أوْحَيْنا". The meaning of "رُوحًا مِن أمْرِنا" is: that by which We give life to creation, from Our command, that is: that by which one is guided, and so becomes alive.
And His saying: ﴿ما كُنْتَ تَدْرِي ما الكِتابُ ولا الإيمانُ ولَكِنْ جَعَلْناهُ نُورًا﴾ — He did not say "جَعَلْناهُما" (We made the two of them), because the meaning is: "but We made the Book a light", and it is a guide to faith.
And His saying: ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إلى صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ — and it is read "وَإنَّكَ لَتُهْدى" (you are guided). Whoever reads "لَتَهْدِي", the meaning is: "you guide, by what We have revealed to you, to a straight path". And it is possible that "لَتُهْدى" is an address to the Prophet ﷺ and his community, so that the meaning would be: "you and your community are guided to a straight path", as He said: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1], which is in the position of: "O believing people, when you divorce women".

zajjaj:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿صِراطِ اللَّهِ﴾ is genitive, a badal (substitute) from "صِراطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ"; the meaning is: "and you guide to the path of Allah". "صِراطُ اللَّهِ" in the nominative and "صِراطَ اللَّهِ" in the accusative are also permissible, but I know of no one who read with both or with either of them, so do not read with either of them, because reading is a sunna (established practice) which is not to be contravened, even if what one reads is permissible in grammar.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ القُرى ومَن حَوْلَها﴾ — "أُمُّ القُرى" (the Mother of Towns) is Mecca, and the position of "وَمَن حَوْلَها" is accusative. The meaning is: "so that you may warn the people of the Mother of Towns and those around it", because a town does not reason. Like this is: ﴿واسْألِ القَرْيَةَ الَّتِي كُنّا فِيها﴾ [Yūsuf: 82].
And His saying: ﴿وَتُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ الجَمْعِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾, that is: the day on which people are all resurrected. Then He made known what their state will be on that day, saying: ﴿فَرِيقٌ في الجَنَّةِ وفَرِيقٌ في السَّعِيرِ﴾

zajjaj:8-8.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَهم أُمَّةً واحِدَةً ولَكِنْ يُدْخِلُ مَن يَشاءُ في رَحْمَتِهِ والظّالِمُونَ ما لَهم مِن ولِيٍّ ولا نَصِيرٍ﴾ — "الظّالِمُونَ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
And His saying: ﴿يُدْخِلُ مَن يَشاءُ في رَحْمَتِهِ والظّالِمِينَ أعَدَّ لَهم عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [al-Insān: 31] — the difference between this and the first is that "أعَدَّ لَهم" is a verb, so "الظّالِمِينَ" is made accusative by an implied verb which the overt one explains; the meaning is: "and He threatened the wrongdoers; He has prepared for them a painful punishment".
